CHAPTER 3: SYSTEM OVERVIEW
The OptiSweep Sorter Sweeper system is a tote-to-person, smalls sorting system consisting of three 
main mechanical components (Geek+ P40 V2.0 robots, tippers, and a hospital station), WCS controller, 
and operator interface. This system works in conjunction with the customer's existing sorter.
Once the sorter starts, parcels are directed into totes. When the tote reaches the customer-specified 
weight, number of parcels, or volume, the WCS sends a message to the sorter PLC to stop diverting 
packages. An AGV is triggered via the WCS controller to retrieve the tote. Another AGV places an empty 
tote where the full tote was removed. The WCS then sends a message to the sorter PLC to resume sort-
ation.
Specifically placed QR codes on the floor direct the AGV with the tote  to an open tipper. When the gripper 
on the tipper senses the tote, it pulls the tote onto the tipper, which deposits the parcel into a parcel bag 
via a chute. A bag ID label is generated and placed on the bag by the bagging employee. The bag is then 
placed  on a take-away conveyor. When the tipping cycle is complete and the tote is empty, the WCS 
indicates to the AGV that the task is complete, and the empty tote is removed by the AGV. The AGV re-
enters the sorter area and follows the commands from the WCS on where to go next.
In the event of a mis-sort, bad tip, or tote overload, the WCS directs the AGV to take the tote to the right 
side of the hospital station to be handled by an operator. The AGV then moves to the left side of the hos-
pital station to pick up an empty tote and re-enters the sorter area to await further instructions.

Details and specifications for the Geek+ P40 robots can be found in the  P40A (V2.0) user manual, Docu-

tipping cycle or presses the yellow button to initiate the tipping cycle after the appropriate bag is ready for 
the Surepost packages.

flashing until the cycle for the first tipper is completed. Both buttons can flash if both sides have AGVs 
and are waiting, but as soon as one tip button  is pressed, the opposite button will go stop flashing until

ment.

3.3: HOSPITAL STATION
In the event of a mis-sort, bad tip, or tote overload, the AGV is directed by the WCS to take the tote to a 
hospital station to be manually handled by an operator. A stacklight indicates a tote is present. An oper-
ator uses a scanner (green scanner) to determine the reason the tote was brought to the station.
The AGV brings the tote to the right side (based on the perspective of the operator) of the hospital sta-
tion, then moves to the left side where an operator places an empty tote on the AGV. The AGV will re-
enter the sorter area after it has a tote to return with.

CHAPTER 5: SYSTEM OPERATION
The OptiSweep Sorter Sweeper is operated by the WCS with manual intervention occurring at the tipper 
and hospital stations. The following procedures apply to the tippers and hospital stations.
5.1: STARTING THE SYSTEM
 1.  On the system HMI, navigate to the system API screen:
 2.  Press SYSTEM STARTUP.

5.2: STOPPING THE SYSTEM
NOTE: The system should be shutdown between sorts to allow AGVs to charge.
 1.  On the system HMI, navigate to the system API screen:
 2.  Press SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.
 3.  The AGVs go to a shutdown queue.
5.3: STARTING THE OPERATOR STATION
If the system has been turned off, follow the procedure below to start the system:
 1.  Verify the AGVs are powered on. Reference P40A (V2.0) user manual, Document version: V1.1 
(20231206) for instructions on starting the AGVs.
 2.  Verify the main disconnect is ON.
 3.  At the operator station control panel, if the ESTOP is flashing, pull out the ESTOP and press 
RESET on the HMI screen to clear any faults.
 4.  "Home" every axis: Z1 and A1 (left tipper) and  Z2 and A2 (right tipper):
 a.  Press AUTO REF.
The axis button changes from green to yellow to indicate it is moving. The tipper motor 
moves until it senses the "home" proximity switch, then stops.
 5.  Press CYCLE START. The motor moves from "home" to "ready."
 6.  Place the tipper in AUTO mode. The tipper will wait for the WCS to send instructions.
5.4: STOPPING THE OPERATOR STATION
 1.  Press CYCLE STOP on the operator station main screen.

The following section provide instructions for the startup and shut down of the AGVs, and guidance on

5.8.1: AGV SYSTEM START-UP
Before starting the system, make sure there are enough AGVs without totes in the system. There should 
be nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south

If the system is started without nine totes, an AGV without a tote will need to be moved into the zone that 
is missing an AGV. Make sure to add the AGV to the RMS after moving the AGV.
NOTE: Make sure to start the system 15 minutes before the sort starts.
To start the system:
 1.  Reset the metrics. This makes pulling reports easier.
 2.  Start the system.
 3.  Close out. After close out (Bag Out) is completed, the system goes back to "Running".
 4.  Shut down.

 4.  Perform whatever task needs to be performed as determined by the information in the status 
fields.
 5.  If a tote is going back into the system, put the tote on the induct side (left side) of the station.

5.10: SORTER SCANNER OPERATION
The Zebra scanner is a versatile hand-held device used at the hospital and the sorter. At the hospital, it is 
primarily utilized for adding and removing totes (see "Hospital Station Operation" on the previous page). 
This section focuses on the usage of the scanner at the sorter for managing totes during manual oper-
ations, such as tote replacement, maintenance, repair, and handling damaged totes.
When a tote is manually removed from the sorter stand, it is essential that the tote with the same Tote ID 
is returned to its original position. Failure to do so will require rescanning to properly associate the tote 
with its designated location. Proper scanning ensures that the system recognizes the correct placement 
and avoids operational errors.

7.2.3: Z-AXIS CABLE CARRIER
The following components should be inspected:
 1.  Inspect the cable carrier for links that have come loose or disconnected or otherwise are not 
uniform.
 2.  Crossbars on the outer radius can sometimes open. Inspect for open or missing crossbars.
 3.  Inspect the air line tie wraps at each end of the cable carrier to ensure they are still intact.
 4.  Inspect the FFC and FFC clamps for any damage.
 5.  Push/pull the cable carrier bracket to ensure it is not mechanically loose.
 6.  Push/pull the cable carrier ends to ensure they are not mechanically loose.
 7.  Visually inspect the cable carrier bracket to make sure it is not bent. The cable carrier should 
form a “U” shape and not curve to a side.
7.2.4: A-AXIS CABLE CARRIER
The following components should be inspected:
 1.  Inspect the cable carrier for links that have come loose, disconnected, or otherwise are not uni-
form.
 2.  Crossbars on the outer radius can sometimes open. Inspect for open or missing crossbars.
 3.  Inspect the air line and cable tie wraps at each end of the cable carrier to ensure they are still 
intact.
 4.  Inspect the cable at both exits to ensure no damage.
 5.  Push/pull the cable carrier bracket to ensure it is not mechanically loose.
 6.  Push/pull the cable carrier ends to ensure they are not mechanically loose.
 7.  Verify the cable carrier bracket  it is not bent. The cable carrier should form a “C” shape in one 
plane and not deviate more than ~1/2 in. from that plane.

 a.  Inspect for cables that have come loose and are hanging or damaged.

 11.  Load firmware.
 12.  Validate setup.

7.3.25: AFTER A POWER OUTAGE
If there is a power outage in the middle of a sort that is long enough for systems to lose communication, 
the following will need to be performed:
 1.  On the System HMI, navigate to the "ACB API" screen.
 2.  In the “System” section, press SYSTEM PURGE.
All of the AGVs with totes will go to operator stations, and the totes will be emptied. Labels will not be prin-
ted for bags, so the packages will need to be re-circulated to the sorter lane.

Figure 4-12: AGV API Controls Controls Description Remove AGV An AGV can be removed from the system by entering the AGV ID. If and AGV has an issue, it must be physically removed from the system. If the AGV has a tote, it must be taken to the hospital where the tote is removed. The tote is then "recovered" when it is put back in the system. Recover AGV Enter an AGV ID to add it to the system. Pause All AGVs Pauses all AGV movement. Resume All AGVs Resumes all AGV movement. Execute AGV Command This is used for a system recover in the event that the system goes down and messages are missed. Resend Geek Com- mand This is also used for a system recover. If Geek+ has a command error, the command guide can be provided and the message will be resent to Geek+. Table 4-2: AVG API Controls Clicking GET AGV STATUS pops up a screen with details about each AGV, including battery status, command status, error codes, and the state of each AGV.

content.text: Figure 4-9: System API Controls 4.1.1: System HMI Screens 22 Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 4.1.1.5.1: SYSTEM API CONTROLS The state of the system can be found in the System section of the API screen. The system can also be started, shut down, and purged using this section of the screen. Figure 4-9: System API Controls Control Description Get System State Displays the current state of OptiSweep. System Startup Allows the user to put the system in a running state. System Shutdown Shuts down the system. The AGVs go to a shutdown queue. This should only be done when a sort does not begin when the current sort ends. System Close Out All totes are sent to the tippers to close out the sorter. Close Out should only be done at the end of a sort. System Purge All totes are sent to the tippers. Labels are not printed during a purge. Reset Metrics Reset the metrics. This should only be done between sorts. content.text: Figure 5-1: System in Shut-down Mode 5.8: AGV Faults 72 Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 5.8: AGV FAULTS The following section provide instructions for the startup and shut down of the AGVs, and guidance on recovering AGVs from their faulted states to get them back in service. 5.8.1: AGV SYSTEM START-UP Before starting the system, make sure there are enough AGVs without totes in the system. There should be nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack. Figure 5-1: System in Shut-down Mode If the system is started without nine totes, an AGV without a tote will need to be moved into the zone that is missing an AGV. Make sure to add the AGV to the RMS after moving the AGV. NOTE: Make sure to start the system 15 minutes before the sort starts. To start the system: 1. Reset the metrics. This makes pulling reports easier. 2. Start the system. 3. Close out. After close out (Bag Out) is completed, the system goes back to "Running". 4. Shut down.

content.text: Figure 5-2: AGV "Bump" Fault Screen 5.8.2: Fault Recovery Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 73 5.8.2: FAULT RECOVERY Before going inside the grid (a.k.a. the Dance Floor), make sure to have the following information: l Robot ID l Fault description from RMS l Does RMS think the faulted AVG is holding a bin? If so, what tote ID? l If faulted AGV is under a rack, is that AGV the empty AGV for that zone? The following sections provide instructions for the recovery process when Geek+ cannot recover the AGV. 5.8.2.1: "BUMP" FAULT CODE Figure 5-2: AGV "Bump" Fault Screen Exception Code Exception Information 21057 Robot front collision bar triggers. 21060 The robot triggers the obstacle avoidance. Table 5-1: AGV Exception Codes 1. E-stop the RMS. 2. Remove the obstruction. 3. Click the AGV RESET button for two (2) seconds to clear the fault. 4. Press E-stop again. 5. Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.)

content.text: Figure 5-3: Add AGV to Zone with No Empty AGV Screen 5.8.2: Fault Recovery 74 Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 5.8.2.2: ADD AGV TO ZONE WITH NO EMPTY AGV Figure 5-3: Add AGV to Zone with No Empty AGV Screen 1. E-stop RMS. 2. Move an AGV into the zone under the tote rack. 3. Add AGV in RMS. (See "Tote API Controls" on page 26.) 4. Wait for AGV to turn blue. 5. Verify AGV status is "szonestaging". (Reference AGV state on HMI.). If the AGV is moving to the Hospital, remove the AGV and add it again. 6. Press E-stop again. 7. Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.) 5.8.2.3: AGVS LOST TASKS If empty AGVs have lost their tasks because the RMS was restarted: 1. E-stop RMS. 2. Remove and re-add AGVs without totes twice. (See "Tote API Controls" on page 26.) 3. If the system needs to be restarted, make sure the AGVs are in the "szonestaging" state. (Reference AGV state on the HMI.) 4. Press the E-stop again when ready to resume. 5. Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.) NOTE: The best practice is to shut down and restart to ensure everything is in sync.

content.text: Figure 7-12: End Stop 7.3.12: End Stop Assembly Replacement Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 139 7.3.12: END STOP ASSEMBLY REPLACEMENT Note that the end stops typically work in pairs. In most cases, a collision at the bottom means there is also a collision at the top. This means a damaged end stop at the bottom suggests one of the top end stops is also damaged. An exception to this could be in the event of a belt failure. Required Tools l Replacement Parts: End stop, two (2) M8x40 socket-head cap screws (per end stop) l PPE: Safety glasses, gloves l Tools Needed: 3/8-in. wrench or socket, 6-mm hex wrench, LoctiteÂ® l Time Required: 15 minutes Figure 7-12: End Stop 7.3.12.1: REPLACEMENT 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2). 2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor. 3. Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place. END S TOPS END S TOPS M8x40 SOCKE T-HEAD SCREWS M8x40 SOCKE T-HEAD SCREWS 4. Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and LoctiteÂ®. 5. Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary.

content.text: None 5.2: Stopping The System 66 Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 5.2: STOPPING THE SYSTEM NOTE: The system should be shutdown between sorts to allow AGVs to charge. 1. On the system HMI, navigate to the system API screen: 2. Press SYSTEM SHUTDOWN. 3. The AGVs go to a shutdown queue. 5.3: STARTING THE OPERATOR STATION If the system has been turned off, follow the procedure below to start the system: 1. Verify the AGVs are powered on. Reference P40A (V2.0) user manual, Document version: V1.1 (20231206) for instructions on starting the AGVs. 2. Verify the main disconnect is ON. 3. At the operator station control panel, if the ESTOP is flashing, pull out the ESTOP and press RESET on the HMI screen to clear any faults. 4. "Home" every axis: Z1 and A1 (left tipper) and Z2 and A2 (right tipper): a. Press AUTO REF. The axis button changes from green to yellow to indicate it is moving. The tipper motor moves until it senses the "home" proximity switch, then stops. 5. Press CYCLE START. The motor moves from "home" to "ready." 6. Place the tipper in AUTO mode. The tipper will wait for the WCS to send instructions. 5.4: STOPPING THE OPERATOR STATION 1. Press CYCLE STOP on the operator station main screen.

content.text: None 5.10.1: Tote Initialization Procedure 78 Â©2025 Fortna Inc. 5.10.1: TOTE INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE To initialize totes at the sorter using the Zebra scanner, follow the procedure below: 1. Open the tote scanning application on the Hospital laptop and select "Sorter Destinations" from the main menu. 2. Approach the sorter and scan the tote sorter stand position barcode. This barcode is located in the center of the rack on the top rail. 3. Scan the tote barcode of the tote being placed in the stand. If the pairing is unsuccessful, the scanner will flash yellow, indicating that rescanning is required. 5. Once the new set of scans is successfully completed, no further action is required. The oper- ator can return the scanner application to Hospital Mode for any subsequent tasks.

Validate connectivity by pinging their IP addresses. Follow the procedure below to setup the new scanner: 1. If red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions.

The OptiSweep Sorter Sweeper system is a tote-to-person, smalls sorting system consisting of three main mechanical components (Geek+ P40 V2.0 robots, tippers, and a hospital station), WCS controller, and operator interface.

Geek+ is the manufacturer of the AGVs. The OptiSweep system uses the Geek+ P40 (V2.0) AVGs. Details and specifications for the Geek+ P40 robots can be found in the P40A (V2.0) user manual, Document version: V1.1 (20231206).

In the event of a mis-sort, bad tip, or tote overload, the WCS directs the AGV to take the tote to the right side of the hospital station to be handled by an operator. The AGV then moves to the left side of the hospital station to pick up an empty tote and re-enters the sorter area to await further instructions.
When the gripper on the tipper senses the tote, it pulls the tote onto the tipper, which deposits the parcel into a parcel bag via a chute.

When the tote reaches the customer-specified weight, number of parcels, or volume, the WCS sends a message to the sorter PLC to stop diverting packages. An AGV is triggered via the WCS controller to retrieve the tote.

Geek+ is the manufacturer of the AGVs. The OptiSweep system uses the Geek+ P40 (V2.0) AVGs. Details and specifications for the Geek+ P40 robots can be found in the P40A (V2.0) user manual, Document version: V1.1 (20231206).

The Tote Exchange Settings interface allows users to view and manage parameters related to the tote exchange process. The system operates in one of three modes: Count, Cube, or Cube & Count.

Figure 4-16: Exchange Settings Pop-Up Screen. Details thresholds: Cube Threshold Pickup, Cube Threshold Priority, Cube Threshold Close, Count Threshold Pickup, Count Threshold Priority, Count Threshold Close, Maximum Weight, Weight Threshold.

The system operates in one of three modes: Count, Cube, or Cube & Count. Count Mode: Exchanges totes based on the number of items in the tote. Cube Mode: Exchanges totes based on the total volume (cube) of all items. Cube & Count Mode: Uses both criteria for exchange decisions.

Cube Threshold Pickup: The cube value at which an AGV can pick up a tote. Cube Threshold Priority: The cube value at which the exchange is prioritized. Cube Threshold Close: The cube value at which the chute should close. Count Threshold Pickup: The item count at which an AGV can pick up a tote. Count Threshold Priority: The item count at which the exchange is prioritized. Count Threshold Close: The item count at which the chute should close. Maximum Weight: The total weight limit that triggers chute closure to prevent overloading. Weight Threshold: The weight value at which the chute should close.

rough_steps: Open the Operator Station HMI VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen. [Image support needed: screenshot/figure of the VISU_MDS Machine Data screen showing the axis parameter list/table and axis selection.]

content.text: A tipper preventive maintenance step to check both Z-axis linear rails for wet grease or dried grease, and if dry, lubricate the bearing blocks via the grease nipples with automotive bearing grease.

structured_payload.title: Inspect and Lubricate Tipper Z-Axis Linear Bearings (Grease Wetness on Z-Axis Linear Rails)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Visually inspect the Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness/dried grease and lubricate bearing blocks if the rails are dry.
structured_payload.summary: A tipper preventive maintenance step to check both Z-axis linear rails for wet grease or dried grease, and if dry, lubricate the bearing blocks via the grease nipples with automotive bearing grease.
rough_steps: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease.
If the rails are dry (not wet with grease), lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1).
Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).
Add 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block.

Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the Z-axis linear rails and bearing blocks/grease nipples location if available in the manual.]
structured_payload.expected_result: Rails show grease wetness after lubrication (when they were initially dry), and grease is applied to each bearing block via the four (4) 1/4-in grease nipples with a total of 1.0 to 3.0 cc per block; wiping alone is not used as the method.
failure_or_escalation_notes: If rails show signs of dried grease but lubrication cannot be performed as specified (e.g., inability to access nipples), stop and escalate to maintenance support.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to both Z-axis linear rails and the bearing blocks
Grease applicator capable of delivering 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block

structured_payload.title: Remove and replace a Limit/Home sensor (A-axis or Z-axis) with LOTO
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Safely remove a defective Limit/Home proximity sensor (A-axis or Z-axis) and prepare the sensor for replacement by unplugging it and removing its mounting hardware.
structured_payload.summary: This procedure describes how to perform LOTO on the tipper, unplug the limit/home sensor, and remove the sensor from its mounting location (A-axis near the A-axis motor PCA; Z-axis inside the CLINK controller in the control box).
rough_steps: Perform LOTO on the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the Operator Station Lockout/Tagout controls referenced by the manual, if available in this packet.]
Unplug the sensor.
Identify sensor type by location: A-axis sensors are plugged into a printed circuit assembly (PCA) near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.

Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed the sensor through the hole where the wire is routed. [Image support needed: Diagram of the Controller PCA (Printed Circuit Assembly) and its mounting box within the OptiSweep tipper station.]
For Z-axis sensors: pull the Z-axis sensor from the column.

For A-axis sensors: pull the defective A-axis sensor away; if needed, cut the wire tie to free the sensor. [Image support needed: close-up showing the M3 button-head screw, the wire routing hole, and the wire tie location.]
structured_payload.expected_result: The defective limit/home sensor is physically removed from its mounting location, its electrical connection is unplugged, and (for A-axis) any wire tie blocking removal is cut if required.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be unplugged or removed without forcing (risk of damaging the PCA/CLINK controller wiring or the wire routing).
Escalate if LOTO cannot be completed or the tipper lockout/tagout controls are not accessible/clear.

Replacement part: Limit sensor or home sensor

rough_steps: Confirm you have two people available and the required PPE/tools: safety glasses, gloves; 16-mm hex wrench; 3/8-in. wrench/socket; replacement part CB weights. structured_payload.title: Remove OptiSweep Gripper at the Operator Station (LOTO + Disconnect Valve/Air/Cables)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Safely stop the cycle, lock out the tipper, and disconnect the gripper hardware (valve cover, air line, M8 connectors, and A-axis cable carrier) to prepare for gripper replacement.
structured_payload.summary: This procedure describes how to stop the cycle from the operator station HMI, perform LOTO at the station e-panel, and disconnect the gripper’s valve cover, air line, electrical connectors, and A-axis cable carrier so the gripper can be removed.
rough_steps: At the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen. [Image support needed: screenshot/photo of the Visu_MCP_Dual screen showing the CYCLE STOP and JOG controls.]
Press CYCLE STOP to stop the cycle, then press JOG to manually control the tipper. [Image support needed: Visu_MCP_Dual screen showing CYCLE STOP and JOG controls.]
Use the axis buttons for the corresponding tipper to move the gripper to the desired location. [Image support needed: Visu_MCP_Dual screen showing the axis buttons for the corresponding tipper.]

If the gripper is moved from its home position, thread screws into the threaded holes in the column to support the carriages between the pair or holes. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the threaded holes in the column and the support screws location.]
LOTO the tipper at the station e-panel. [Image support needed: photo/figure of the station e-panel lockout/tagout location or label referenced by the manual.]
Verify the correct gripper has been selected (left gripper or right gripper). [Image support needed: Visu_MCP_Dual or related UI element indicating left vs right gripper selection.]

Remove the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws from the valve cover, then remove the valve cover. [Image support needed: close-up showing valve cover, M4x50 socket-head screws, and the valve cover removal area.]
Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors. [Image support needed: close-up showing the four M8 connectors labeled/located on the valve/gripper assembly.]
Disconnect the supply air line on the top of the valve. [Image support needed: close-up showing the air line connection on top of the valve.]

Plug the fitting and cap the air line to prevent debris from entering either; if plugs/caps are not available, use tape to protect both. [Image support needed: photo showing capped air line and plugged fitting.]
Feed the capped air line through the grommet. [Image support needed: photo showing the grommet and the air line passing through it.]
Pull the jacketed part of the cable out of the grommet. [Image support needed: photo showing jacketed cable being pulled through the grommet.]
Feed all of the M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time. [Image support needed: photo showing M8 connectors routed through the grommet.]

Detach the A-axis cable carrier from the gripper by removing the two (2) M3x8 screws holding the cable carrier end. Save the screws. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the A-axis cable carrier end and the two M3x8 screws.]
Install the valve cover using the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws. [Image support needed: photo showing valve cover reinstalled with M4x50 screws.]

Remove the 10 M6x20 socket-head screws attaching the gripper to the gearbox (suggested: fully remove nine (9) screws). Ensure the counter-balance is supported. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the gripper-to-gearbox screw locations and counter-balance support point.]

failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and escalate if you cannot confirm the correct gripper selection (left vs right) before disconnecting hardware.
Stop and escalate if the counter-balance cannot be supported while removing the gripper-to-gearbox screws.
Stop and escalate if plugs/caps (or tape protection) cannot be applied to prevent debris entering the air line/fitting.

content.text: A hands-on installation procedure for OptiSweep timing belt replacement, including counter-balance positioning, equal tensioning of two screws, sonic tension meter settings, and final torque/fastener steps before restarting the operator station.

structured_payload.title: Install and tension a replacement timing belt (counter-balance leg) to 471 N
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Replace the timing belt and set belt tension to the specified target so the belt is properly tensioned and secured before reassembly and operator-station restart.
structured_payload.summary: A hands-on installation procedure for OptiSweep timing belt replacement, including counter-balance positioning, equal tensioning of two screws, sonic tension meter settings, and final torque/fastener steps before restarting the operator station.
rough_steps: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys.
Slightly lift the counter-balance carriage, remove the M6 fastener supporting it, and lower the counter-balance carriage to rest on the lower hard stop.

Very lightly tighten the M8x25 screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place so the assembly is not loose, but it can slide under the fasteners. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the idler pulley assembly and the M8x25 screws location.]
Insert the two M6x35 tension screws until they make firm contact with the actuator base. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the two M6x35 tension screws and actuator base contact point.]
Equally tighten the tension screws to add tension to the belt, ensuring both screws are turned the exact same amount (same applied force).
Gradually increase tension until 471 N is reached (acceptable range 448 N to 494 N).
Check tension only on the counter-balance leg of the belt (counter-balance is not in the way and will not interfere with belt vibration).

If using a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, set: Mass = 4.86 g/m, Width = 20 mm, Span = 1200 mm. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter settings screen/controls.]
Adjust/check until three acceptable readings in a row are received. Note: excessive noise (e.g., forklifts beeping, conveyors running) can interfere with sonic meter readings.
Tighten the M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs) to lock the idler assembly in place.

Raise the counter-balance carriage back to mid-travel and insert the M6 socket-head screws for the carriage to rest against. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the M6 socket-head screws and mid-travel rest position.]

Re-attach the A-axis belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring the belt clamp aligns with belt teeth and does not pinch the belt (belt may need slight movement to line up). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the A-axis belt clamp alignment with belt teeth.]

Re-attach the counter-balance belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch (counter-balance may need to be lifted slightly for alignment). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the counter-balance belt clamp alignment.]
Remove the M6 socket-head screws supporting the A-axis and counter-balance.
Reinstall the side panels.
Re-start the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
structured_payload.expected_result: Belt tension is set to 471 N within the acceptable range (448–494 N), tension readings are acceptable for three consecutive checks (if using the sonic meter), idler assembly is locked by tightening M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs), and belt clamps are aligned with belt teeth without pinching before operator-station restart.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and re-check if tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range or if three consecutive acceptable sonic meter readings cannot be obtained.
Stop and re-check clamp alignment if the belt appears pinched or the belt clamp does not align with belt teeth.
If excessive noise prevents stable sonic readings, reduce noise sources and re-check tension.

Torque tool capable of 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs)
Fasteners/tools for M6x35, M8x25, and M6x20 screws

structured_payload.title: Remove Tip (or A-Axis) Cable From Tipper/A-Axis Carriage
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Safely remove the Tip (or A-Axis) cable from the tipper station by disconnecting the four M8 connectors, opening the snap-open cable carrier, cutting cable ties, and unplugging from the A-axis PCA.
structured_payload.summary: This procedure describes LOTO and physical removal of the Tip (A-Axis) cable, including removing the side panel and valve cover, disconnecting M8 connectors, routing through the grommet, opening the cable carrier, cutting ties, and unplugging from the A-axis PCA.
rough_steps: Perform LOTO on the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the tipper lockout/tagout location or the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout page if available in this packet.]

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping screws securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: Diagram showing the routing path for the Tip (A-Axis) cable inside the OptiSweep tipper station.]
Remove the valve cover by removing the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws. [Image support needed: close-up/figure showing the valve cover and the four M4x50 socket-head screws.]
Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors. [Image support needed: figure showing the four M8 connections on the A-axis carriage.]
Pull the jacketed part of the cable out of the grommet, then feed all the M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time.
Open all of the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier (snap-open type). [Image support needed: figure showing the snap-open cable carrier cross bars.]
Use tape or a marker to mark the cable on both ends where the cable enters the cable carrier.

Note how the cable ties are situated at both ends of the carrier (take a picture) and cut the cable ties holding the cable to the cable carrier at both ends and the tie point on the A-axis carriage. [Image support needed: figure showing cable tie locations at both ends of the carrier and the tie point on the A-axis carriage.]

Unplug the cable from the A-axis PCA and remove it from the cable carrier. There may be one more cable tie to cut near the PCA. [Image support needed: figure showing the A-axis PCA connection point and nearby tie location.]
Transfer the markings from Step 5 to the new cable.
structured_payload.expected_result: The Tip (or A-Axis) cable is fully disconnected and removed: all four M8 connectors are disconnected and routed through the grommet, the cable carrier cross bars are opened, cable ties at both carrier ends and the A-axis carriage tie point are cut, and the cable is unplugged from the A-axis PCA with the cable removed from the carrier.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and re-check if any M8 connectors remain connected or if the cable cannot be pulled free after opening the cable carrier cross bars.
Stop and re-check if the cable is still attached by an uncut cable tie near the A-axis PCA (the procedure notes there may be one more tie to cut near the PCA).
Escalate to FORTNA support if LOTO cannot be completed or if access to the motor/valve cover cannot be achieved as described.

rough_steps: Plug the new cable into the A-axis PCA and route the cable around the gearbox and into and around the cable carrier. [Image support needed: diagram/photo showing the cable routing around the gearbox and into the cable carrier.]
Close all the cross bars, ensuring the dividers are between the cable and air line. [Image support needed: view showing cross bars closed and dividers positioned between cable and air line.]

Align the cable markings to the cable carrier and wire-tie in place as before, including both ends of the cable carrier and the tie point on the A-axis carriage. [Image support needed: cable markings alignment and wire tie points at both cable carrier ends and A-axis carriage tie point.]

Near the A-axis PCA, ensure no wires are dangling; use wire ties as needed to contain the cable. [Image support needed: close-up of A-axis PCA area showing no dangling wires and wire ties securing the cable.]

Route all four M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time, then finish by pushing the end of the jacketed cable through the grommet. [Image support needed: grommet and M8 connectors passing through it; show jacketed cable end pushed through.]
Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "Valve" to the valve. [Image support needed: labeled "Valve" 3-pin M8 connector connected to the valve.]
Connect the 4-pin M8 connector to the tote detect sensor. [Image support needed: 4-pin M8 connector connected to tote detect sensor.]
Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "LONG" to the longer gripper sensor. [Image support needed: labeled "LONG" 3-pin M8 connector connected to longer gripper sensor.]
Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "SHORT" to the shorter gripper sensor. [Image support needed: labeled "SHORT" 3-pin M8 connector connected to shorter gripper sensor.]

Install the valve cover using the four M4x50 socket-head screws; make sure not to pinch any wires along the edges of the cover, and insert the grommet into the notch for the tote sensor wire. failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and re-check wiring/routing if any wires are dangling near the A-axis PCA, if the dividers are not positioned between the cable and air line, if the grommet is not seated into the notch for the tote sensor wire, or if wires appear pinched at the valve cover edges.

structured_payload.candidate_goal: Replace the Z-axis cable carrier quickly when both ends of the existing carrier are in good condition, restoring the carrier to the tipper with the cross bars and end pieces properly snapped in.
structured_payload.summary: Performs a quick Z-axis cable carrier replacement by LOTO the tipper, snapping the carrier apart at both ends, removing the old carrier, installing the new carrier, snapping cross bars closed, and snapping both ends into the end pieces that remain mounted.
rough_steps: Perform LOTO on the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the tipper lockout/tagout points or the referenced “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” location if available in this manual.]

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the station side panel and the nine (9) self-tapping securing points.]

structured_payload.title: Perform Full Replacement of the Z-Axis Cable Carrier (without replacing air line or FFC)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Replace the Z-axis cable carrier end-to-end while preserving the existing air line and FFC, then verify the carrier is seated and restart the operator station.
structured_payload.summary: A full cable-carrier replacement procedure for the Z-axis that includes LOTO, disconnecting and reinstalling the carrier, verifying cross bars/dividers/joints, and restarting the operator station.
rough_steps: Apply LOTO to the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the tipper lockout/tagout location and method if available in the manual.]

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the nine self-tapping fasteners and side panel.]

Mark the air line and FFC at both ends where they enter and exit the cable carrier using marker or tape. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing where the air line and FFC enter/exit the cable carrier.]
Note how the air line is tied to the cable carrier (take a picture) and cut the wire ties. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the air line tie/wire-tie points.]

At both ends of the cable carrier, remove the M3 socket-head screws holding the FFC clamps in place. Confirm the clamps should stay in place on the FFC; if they fall off, mark the FFC. [Image support needed: close-up showing M3 socket-head screws and FFC clamps.]
Detach the cable carrier by removing the four M3 screws at both ends of the cable carrier. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the four M3 screws per end.]

Open all cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier and remove it from the FFC and air line. If needed, snap one end of the cable carrier off to fully remove it. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing cross bars and how to snap an end.]

On the new cable carrier, open all cross bars and position it roughly in place while positioning internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing internal dividers placement against the air line.]

“Snap” all cross bars closed, ensuring none of the dividers are pressing on the FFC; snap the end back on if necessary. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing cross bars snapped closed and divider clearance from FFC.]
Mount both ends using four M3 flat-head screws. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing M3 flat-head screws at both ends.]

Attach the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws at both cable carrier ends; ensure the FFC clamps align with the marks from Step 1. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing clamp alignment to marks.]
Position the air line in the cable carrier using the marks from Step 1 and wire-tie it in place. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing air line routing and wire-tie points.]

Inspect the cable carrier: verify all cross bars are closed, dividers are not pressing on the FFC, and all cable carrier joints are fully seated. The cable carrier should look very uniform end to end. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing “uniform end to end” appearance and joint seating.]
Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels if necessary. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing top/bottom side panels.]
Re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66). [Image support needed: screenshot/figure of the operator station start control if available.]
structured_payload.expected_result: The new Z-axis cable carrier is installed with all cross bars closed, dividers not pressing on the FFC, joints fully seated (uniform end-to-end appearance), and the operator station is restarted successfully.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and re-check alignment/clearance if dividers are pressing on the FFC or if cable carrier joints do not appear fully seated/uniform end-to-end.
If the FFC clamps did not stay in place during removal and the FFC was not marked, stop and correct clamp alignment before proceeding.
If the operator station does not restart after reassembly, escalate to the appropriate support process (manual references “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).

3/8-in. wrench or socket (if needed to remove the nine self-tapping securing the station side panel)

structured_payload.title: Remove Timing Pulley (LOTO + side panel access + taper-lock bushing set-screw release)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Safely remove the timing pulley assembly from the gearbox by performing lockout/tagout, accessing the motor, and breaking the pulley free from the 1108 taper-lock bushing without damaging gearbox bearings.
structured_payload.summary: A mechanical removal procedure for the timing pulley assembly that includes LOTO, side panel removal for motor access, and set-screw steps to release the pulley from the taper-lock bushing.
rough_steps: Perform LOTO on the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/diagram showing the tipper lockout/tagout points referenced by the manual’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” section.]

If necessary, remove the station side panel to access the motor: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the station side panel and the nine (9) self-tapping fasteners.]
Remove both set screws from the 1108 taper-lock bushing using an 1/8-in. hex wrench. [Image support needed: close-up of the 1108 taper-lock bushing showing the two set screws.]

Thread one (1) set screw into the hole between the holes that held the set screws (the hole has threads on the taper-lock bushing side and is smooth on the pulley side). [Image support needed: diagram/photo indicating the “hole between the holes” and which side is threaded vs smooth.]

Tighten the set screw to break the pulley free from the taper-lock bushing (may take some work). [Image support needed: figure showing the pulley seated in the taper-lock bushing and the expected separation after tightening.]

Once the pulley is free, verify that everything should slide off the shaft. Do NOT hit the pulley with a hammer (this will damage the bearings in the gearbox). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the pulley removed/clear of the shaft and gearbox pilot face alignment context.]
structured_payload.expected_result: After tightening the threaded set screw, the timing pulley is free from the 1108 taper-lock bushing and the pulley assembly slides off the shaft; the procedure avoids hammering to prevent gearbox bearing damage.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and escalate if the pulley does not break free after tightening the set screw (do not hammer the pulley).
Stop if you cannot access the motor due to side panel fasteners not being removed as specified (nine (9) self-tapping fasteners).

structured_payload.title: Install Timing Pulley Using Taper Lock Bushing (Timing Pulley Replacement 7.3.19.2)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Correctly install the timing pulley with the taper lock bushing so the pulley is positioned at the specified 8 mm distance from the gearbox pilot face and the set screws are torqued to the specified value.
structured_payload.summary: A site/operator-executable installation procedure for the timing pulley replacement that specifies alignment, spacing, and set-screw torque, then re-starts the operator station.
rough_steps: Loosely assemble the taper lock bushing into the pulley and align all three holes.
Thread set screws into the two holes that are opposite each other; the set screws should have threads on the pulley half and be smooth on the bushing half.
Slip the assembly onto the shaft with the keyway slot aligned with the gearbox shaft key (if present).

Tighten in place and verify the final position of the pulley is 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face; use a spacer between the gearbox pilot face and pulley to maintain the spacing. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the 8 mm (0.315 in.) measurement location between gearbox pilot face and pulley.]

In small increments, tighten both set screws, alternating between them until the set screw torque reaches 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing set screws and where torque is applied.]
Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66). [Image support needed: screenshot/photo of the operator station start control(s) referenced on page 66.]
structured_payload.expected_result: The timing pulley is seated with the keyway aligned to the gearbox shaft key (if present), the pulley-to-gearbox pilot face spacing is 8 mm (0.315 in.), and both set screws are torqued to 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb); side panels are reinstalled and the operator station is restarted.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and re-check alignment/spacing if the pulley final position is not 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face.
Stop and re-torque if the set screw torque does not reach 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb) after alternating tightening in small increments.
If the operator station does not restart successfully after reassembly, escalate to support and reference the "Starting The Operator Station" procedure on page 66.

content.text: This procedure covers the live-system safety and mechanical positioning steps required before removing the idler pulley assembly: lockout/tagout the tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor, and manually position the A-axis/counterbalance with M6 socket-head screws threaded into the specified holes to prevent dropping.

structured_payload.title: Replace OptiSweep Idler Pulley Assembly — LOTO tipper and prevent A-axis/counterbalance drop during removal
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Safely prepare the tipper for idler pulley assembly removal by performing lockout/tagout and mechanically preventing the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping when belt tension is released.
structured_payload.summary: This procedure covers the live-system safety and mechanical positioning steps required before removing the idler pulley assembly: lockout/tagout the tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor, and manually position the A-axis/counterbalance with M6 socket-head screws threaded into the specified holes to prevent dropping.
rough_steps: Identify the specific tipper station to be serviced and perform LOTO on the tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).

If needed to access the motor, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel. [Image support needed: Maintenance diagram of the idler pulley assembly for the OptiSweep tipper.]

Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base: there are two holes adjacent to each rail, and the carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.
Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

Stop if LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper or if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified holes; escalate to FORTNA support or follow the site’s safety escalation process.
structured_payload.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out, the station side panel (if removed) exposes the motor, and the A-axis/counterbalance is mechanically restrained by M6 socket-head screws threaded into the holes below both carriages (with carriages positioned between the two holes adjacent to each rail).
failure_or_escalation_notes: Escalate if LOTO cannot be performed on the intended tipper station.
Escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

LOTO capability per the manual’s "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure
Idler pulley assembly replacement part (for the overall job)

structured_payload.title: Remove Idler Pulley Assembly (A-axis / counterbalance belt system) on a LOTOed tipper
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Safely remove the idler pulley assembly from the tipper’s A-axis/counterbalance belt system by following the documented LOTO and mechanical positioning steps to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
structured_payload.summary: Operator performs LOTO, opens the station side panel if needed, positions the A-axis and counterbalance using the actuator base threaded holes, secures them with M6 socket-head screws, releases belt tension, and slides the idler pulley assembly out of the column.
rough_steps: Perform LOTO on the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the tipper lockout/tagout points or the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout page if available.]

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the station side panel and the nine self-tapping screws location.]

Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base: there are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails. [Image support needed: Figure 7-21 showing A-axis/counterbalance carriage positions relative to the threaded holes on the actuator base.]

Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released. [Image support needed: Figure 7-21 showing where the M6 socket-head screws are threaded below the carriages.]

Remove the belt clamps by removing the six (6) M6x20 countersunk screws with a 5-mm hex wrench from each clamp to free the carriages from the belt. [Image support needed: Figure 7-21 showing belt clamps and the M6x20 countersunk screws.]
Release belt tension by loosening the two (2) M6x35 socket-head screws on the bottom side of the assembly. [Image support needed: Figure 7-21 showing the bottom-side M6x35 tensioning screws.]

Remove the two (2) M8x25 socket-head screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place, then slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column. If needed, transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws from the removed idler pulley assembly to the new assembly. [Image support needed: Figure 7-21 showing the M8x25 mounting screws and the slide-out direction/location of the idler pulley assembly.]
structured_payload.expected_result: With the tipper LOTOed and the A-axis/counterbalance secured, belt clamps are removed, belt tension is released, and the idler pulley assembly is unfastened (M8x25 screws removed) and slid out of the column; if required, the M6x35 tensioning screws are transferred to the new assembly.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance is not held securely by the threaded M6 socket-head screws before loosening belt tension (risk of dropping).
Stop and escalate if the idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 socket-head screws (possible remaining fasteners or misalignment).

structured_payload.summary: This procedure describes how to replace the tipper on an OptiSweep operator station: lockout/tagout, remove access panels as needed, disconnect the control box and tipper connections (power, Ethernet, air), remove the old tipper from the sub-plate, and install the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate.
rough_steps: Perform LOTO on the tipper. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the operator station lockout/tagout location or the tipper lockout/tagout method referenced by the manual.]

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the station side panel and the nine self-tapping securing screws.]

Remove the control box and disconnect the power cable from the tipper (6-pin Molex connector), then push the cable into the column. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the control box, the 6-pin Molex connector, and where the cable is pushed into the column.]

Unplug the Ethernet cable from the ClearLink controller and push the Ethernet cable into the column. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the ClearLink controller Ethernet port and the cable routing into the column.]

Disconnect the air line at the quick disconnect at the bottom of the column, leaving the quick disconnect with the tipper side of the air line. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the air line quick disconnect at the bottom of the column and which side remains attached.]
Add tape over the air line and quick disconnect to prevent debris from entering either side of the air line.

Install the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate.
Connect the conduit, power, air, and Ethernet to the column and control box.
Mount the gripper if necessary.
Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels if necessary.

Re-start the operator station. [Image support needed: photo/figure or UI reference showing how to start/restart the operator station (manual section referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 1).]

rough_steps: Perform LOTO of the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: Diagram of the Flat-Flex Cable (FFC) used in the OptiSweep tipper's A-axis PCA.]
Starting at the A-axis PCA, remove the four (4) M3 socket-head screws holding the two (2) FFC clamps.
Unplug the old FFC from the A-axis PCA connection point.
Plug in the new FFC.
Reinstall the FFC clamps and secure them using the M3 socket-head screws.

Verify the FFC clamps are reinstalled with the four M3 socket-head screws at the A-axis PCA. [Image support needed: Figure 7-14 showing the FFC clamps, M3 socket-head screws, and the A-axis PCA connection point.]
structured_payload.expected_result: The new flat-flex cable (FFC) is plugged in at the A-axis PCA and secured by the two FFC clamps using the four M3 socket-head screws, with the station side panel reinstalled if it was removed.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Do not install the wrong controller hardware: left and right ClearLink controllers have the same hardware but are not interchangeable because IP addresses differ; ensure the correct controller/FFC assembly is installed as applicable.
If the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged or clamps cannot be resecured with the M3 socket-head screws, stop and escalate for further guidance.

content.text: Loosely assemble taper lock bushing into the pulley, thread and align set screws, slip assembly onto the shaft with keyway alignment, position pulley 8 mm from gearbox pilot face, then tighten set screws in alternating increments to 5.6 Nm. Reinstall side panels if needed and restart the operator station.

structured_payload.title: 7.3.19.2 Installation: Timing Pulley replacement (taper lock bushing + pulley set screws)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Install the timing pulley using a taper lock bushing, align the keyway, set the pulley spacing from the gearbox pilot face, and torque the set screws to the specified value.
structured_payload.summary: Loosely assemble taper lock bushing into the pulley, thread and align set screws, slip assembly onto the shaft with keyway alignment, position pulley 8 mm from gearbox pilot face, then tighten set screws in alternating increments to 5.6 Nm. Reinstall side panels if needed and restart the operator station.
rough_steps: Loosely assemble the taper lock bushing into the pulley and align all three holes.
Thread set screws into the two holes that are opposite each other; confirm the set screws have threads on the pulley half and are smooth on the bushing half.
Slip the assembly onto the shaft with the keyway slot aligned with the gearbox shaft key (if present).
Verify the final pulley position is 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face; place a spacer between the gearbox pilot face and pulley to maintain spacing. Use an 8-mm hex wrench for this task.
In small increments, tighten both set screws, alternating between them until the set screw torque reaches 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb).
Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).
structured_payload.expected_result: Timing pulley assembly is seated with keyway alignment, pulley is positioned 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face, and both opposite set screws are tightened to 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb); side panels are reinstalled (if removed) and the operator station is restarted.
failure_or_escalation_notes: If the pulley cannot be positioned to 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face using a spacer, stop and re-check alignment/spacing before proceeding to set-screw tightening.
If set screw torque cannot be reached to 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb) after alternating incremental tightening, stop and re-check set screw seating and assembly alignment.
access_or_tools_needed: Spacer (between gearbox pilot face and pulley) to maintain 8 mm spacing
Torque tool capable of 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb)
Access to reinstall top and/or bottom side panels (if removed)

structured_payload.title: 7.3.20.1 Idler Pulley Assembly Replacement - Removal (LOTO, side panel access, carriage positioning)
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Prepare the OptiSweep tipper for idler pulley assembly replacement by locking out the system, accessing the motor, and positioning the A-axis/counterbalance to prevent dropping when belt tension is released.
structured_payload.summary: Perform LOTO on the tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor, then manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base and secure them with M6 socket-head screws to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
rough_steps: LOTO the tipper using the procedure referenced as "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2. [Escalation note: do not proceed without completing LOTO.]

If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor. [Image support needed: Maintenance diagram of the idler pulley assembly for the OptiSweep tipper.]

Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base: identify two holes adjacent to each rail, and position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.

Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released. [Image support needed: Figure 7-21 showing the idler pulley assembly and the A-axis/counterbalance carriage positions relative to the threaded holes.]
structured_payload.expected_result: Tipper is LOTO; station side panel is removed (if needed) for motor access; A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail; M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping when belt tension is released.
failure_or_escalation_notes: If the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, stop and escalate before releasing belt tension (the screws are intended to prevent dropping).

structured_payload.title: Load tipper firmware via HMI USB dongle
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Update the tipper controller firmware using a USB drive and then reboot the controller to boot normally and reach the expected HMI screens.
structured_payload.summary: Power-cycle the tipper using the disconnect, enter the HMI gray screen by holding the top three HMI buttons during power-on, install firmware from a USB drive via the HMI INSTALL FROM FILE button, then power the controller off and back on and allow normal boot without pressing buttons; verify the Visu_Default screen appears and navigate to Visu_MCP_Dual using F3.
rough_steps: Turn off power to the tipper using the disconnect.
On the HMI, press and hold the top three buttons. [Image support needed: HMI screenshot showing the Visu_Default screen with IP and subnet mask settings during tipper commissioning.]
While continuing to hold the buttons, power on the tipper.
Hold the buttons until a gray screen appears. [Image support needed: HMI screenshot showing the Visu_Default screen with IP and subnet mask settings during tipper commissioning.]

Plug the USB drive containing the new version of firmware into the USB dongle on the HMI. [Image support needed: HMI screenshot showing the Visu_Default screen with IP and subnet mask settings during tipper commissioning.]
Press the INSTALL FROM FILE button. [Image support needed: HMI screenshot showing the Visu_Default screen with IP and subnet mask settings during tipper commissioning.]
Load the firmware from the USB.
Power the controller off and back on; allow the controller to boot normally and do not press any buttons.

Verify the "Visu_Default" screen appears on the HMI displaying the IP and subnet mask settings. [Image support needed: HMI screenshot showing the Visu_Default screen with IP and subnet mask settings during tipper commissioning.]
Press F3 to go to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen. [Image support needed: HMI screenshot showing the Visu_Default screen with IP and subnet mask settings during tipper commissioning.]
structured_payload.expected_result: After the firmware load and controller reboot, the HMI displays the "Visu_Default" screen showing IP and subnet mask settings, and pressing F3 brings up the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
failure_or_escalation_notes: If the gray screen does not appear while holding the top three HMI buttons during power-on, repeat the button-hold/power-on sequence as described.
If the controller does not boot normally after power off/on (or if buttons are pressed during boot), repeat the power off/on step and ensure no buttons are pressed during boot.

content.text: Safely remove the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox assembly by performing LOTO, removing the station side panel to access the motor, removing the gripper, and controlling counter-balance drift after gripper removal (either allow drift to the lower hard stop or remove the counter-balance weight).

structured_payload.title: Remove A-Axis Gearbox (LOTO, side panel access, gripper removal, counter-balance handling)
structured_payload.summary: Safely remove the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox assembly by performing LOTO, removing the station side panel to access the motor, removing the gripper, and controlling counter-balance drift after gripper removal (either allow drift to the lower hard stop or remove the counter-balance weight).
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox must be removed and you need to follow the manual’s LOTO and disassembly sequence, including managing counter-balance drift risk after gripper removal.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute the physical disassembly steps (LOTO, side panel removal, gripper removal, gearbox unmounting/removal) and control counter-balance drift as specified.
safety_notes: Most fasteners in the A-axis gearbox have Loctite® 277™, so removal may be difficult (use appropriate tools and control unexpected movement).

After gripper removal, the system will be out of balance and the counter-balance will want to drift down; it is acceptable to allow drift to the lower hard stop or optionally remove the counter-balance weight to help balance the system.
If unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the A-axis gearbox area
Tools: torque wrench, 4-mm hex wrench, 3/8-in. wrench/socket, standard screwdriver

access_required: Physical access to the A-axis gearbox area
system_preconditions: System is ready for lockout/tagout per the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.
external_references: Manual cross-reference: "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2 (referenced by the A-axis gearbox removal section).
Manual cross-reference: "Removal" on page 97 for gripper removal.

visual_references.description: Figure 7-6 (A-Axis Gearbox) supporting the A-axis gearbox removal sequence and fastener/tooling context.
Figure 7-7 (Gearbox) showing gearbox assembly context and the manual’s note about Loctite® 277 and positioning/prevention of dropping.

Figure 7-4 (Counterbalance Weight) supporting the optional counter-balance weight removal approach and the note that carriage movement/drift is acceptable as gripper will drift to the lower hard stop.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the system
steps.purpose: Ensure the system is locked out/tagged out before removing the side panel and disassembling the A-axis gearbox.
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the system using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.
steps.expected_result: The system is in a locked-out/tagged-out state prior to side panel removal.
steps.healthy_condition: No unexpected motion occurs when you begin disassembly actions.
steps.failure_condition: Any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly.

actions.label: Execute Operator Station Lockout/Tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the system (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: If any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 1: "LOTO the system (see \"Operator Station Lockout/Tagout\" on page 2)."

steps.title: Remove the station side panel to access the motor
steps.purpose: Expose the motor area by removing the nine self-tapping fasteners securing the station side panel.
steps.instruction: Using a 3/8-in. wrench or socket, remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is removed and the motor access area is exposed.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete without unexpected movement; motor access is visible.
steps.failure_condition: Unexpected motion occurs during side panel removal, or the side panel cannot be removed due to uncontrolled fastener resistance.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: If any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 2: "Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor."
A-axis gearbox note: "Most fasteners in the A-axis gearbox have Loctite® 277™, so removal may be difficult."

steps.title: Remove the gripper
steps.purpose: Remove the gripper as required by the A-axis gearbox removal sequence; this triggers the counter-balance drift condition that must be managed next.
steps.instruction: Remove the gripper (manual cross-reference: "Removal" on page 97).
steps.expected_result: The gripper is removed.
steps.healthy_condition: After gripper removal, you observe the system out-of-balance condition and can control the counter-balance drift as described in the next step.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by the optional counter-balance weight removal approach).

actions.label: Remove gripper
actions.exact_action: Remove the gripper (see "Removal" on page 97).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed), stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 3: "Remove the gripper (see \"Removal\" on page 97)."

steps.title: Control counter-balance drift after gripper removal
steps.purpose: Manage the out-of-balance condition so the counter-balance drift is controlled to the lower hard stop or balanced by removing the counter-balance weight.
steps.instruction: After gripper removal, allow the counter-balance to drift down to the lower hard stop OR remove the counter-balance weight to help balance the system.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance drift is controlled: either it reaches the lower hard stop or the counter-balance weight is removed to balance the system.
steps.healthy_condition: The counter-balance drift proceeds in a controlled manner to the lower hard stop, or the counter-balance weight is removed as an alternative balancing method.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed).

actions.label: Allow drift to lower hard stop
actions.exact_action: It is acceptable to allow it to drift to the lower hard stop, or optionally, the counter-balance weight can be removed to help balance the system.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed), stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 4: "With the gripper removed, the system will be out of balance: the counter-balance will want to drift down. It is acceptable to allow it to drift to the lower hard stop, or optionally, the counter-balance weight can be removed to help balance the system."
Figure 7-4 note: "Once the weights are removed, the carriage may begin to move. The movement is acceptable as the gripper will drift to the lower hard stop."

steps.title: Remove the gearbox without removing the motor (motor may be needed for fastener access)
steps.purpose: Proceed with gearbox removal while noting that motor removal may be required to access fasteners.
steps.instruction: Remove the gearbox without removing the motor; if fastener access requires it, remove the motor (manual cross-reference: "Motor Removal" on page 106).
steps.expected_result: You are positioned to remove the gearbox mounting fasteners; motor removal is only performed if required for fastener access.
steps.healthy_condition: Gearbox mounting fasteners are accessible for removal without unnecessary motor removal.
steps.failure_condition: Fasteners cannot be accessed safely without removing the motor, or removal attempts cause uncontrolled movement.

actions.label: Assess fastener access
actions.exact_action: Remove the gearbox without removing the motor. However, the motor will likely need to be removed for fastener access. See "Motor Removal" on page 106.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access fasteners safely without causing uncontrolled movement, stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 5: "Remove the gearbox without removing the motor. However, the motor will likely need to be removed for fastener access. See \"Motor Removal\" on page 106."

steps.title: Remove the gearbox mounting screws
steps.purpose: Detach the gearbox from the carriage by removing the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws.
steps.instruction: Remove the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws mounting the gearbox to the carriage.
steps.expected_result: All eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws are removed and the gearbox is no longer secured to the carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: No remaining fasteners secure the gearbox; gearbox can be lifted/removed without binding.
steps.failure_condition: Any screw remains engaged, or the gearbox binds due to misalignment or remaining fasteners.

actions.label: Remove gearbox screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws mounting the gearbox to the carriage.

stop_or_escalate_if: If fasteners resist removal due to Loctite® 277 and you cannot remove them without risking uncontrolled movement, stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 6: "Remove the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws mounting the gearbox to the carriage."

steps.title: Remove the gearbox
steps.purpose: Complete the gearbox removal by lifting the gearbox assembly away from the carriage.
steps.instruction: Remove the gearbox.
steps.expected_result: The gearbox is removed from the carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: Gearbox removal completes without unexpected motion of the counter-balance system.
steps.failure_condition: Unexpected motion occurs during gearbox removal, or the gearbox cannot be removed due to remaining attachment points.

actions.label: Lift off gearbox
actions.exact_action: Remove the gearbox.

stop_or_escalate_if: If any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.
If the gearbox cannot be removed cleanly, stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.6.1 REMOVAL step 7: "Remove the gearbox."

success_criteria: Station side panel is removed to access the motor.
Gripper is removed.
Counter-balance drift is controlled: either drift to the lower hard stop or counter-balance weight removed to help balance the system.
Gearbox is unmounted after removing eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws and is removed.
healthy_conditions: No unexpected motion occurs during disassembly.
After gripper removal, counter-balance drift is controlled as specified (lower hard stop or counter-balance weight removal).
All eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws are removed and gearbox removal is unimpeded.
failure_conditions: Unexpected motion occurs during disassembly (indicates LOTO issue).
Counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed).
Gearbox cannot be removed due to remaining attachment points or uncontrolled binding.
escalation_guidance: If counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed), stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.
If unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.

steps.title: E-stop RMS

steps.title: Remove the faulted AGV that is lifted and faulted out while leaving
steps.purpose: Clear the faulted AGV from the RMS so exchange can be re-established.
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), identify the AGV that is lifted and has faulted out while leaving, then remove that AGV from the RMS using the AGV API Controls flow referenced by the manual.
steps.expected_result: The faulted AGV is removed from the RMS (it no longer appears as an active AGV in the RMS fleet context for the affected zone).
steps.healthy_condition: Only the faulted AGV is removed; the RMS remains stopped while you confirm the removal is reflected in the RMS UI.
steps.failure_condition: The faulted AGV cannot be removed from RMS, or it remains present/active in the RMS UI after the removal action.

actions.label: Remove AGV from RMS
actions.exact_action: Remove the AGV that is lifted that has faulted out while leaving from the RMS. (See "AGV API Controls" on page 24.)

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 5.8.2.5: AGV FAULT DURING EXCHANGE: 2. Remove the AGV that is lifted that has faulted out while leaving from the RMS. (See "AGV API Controls" on page 24.)

steps.title: Check backfill; remove trailing AGV if it does not backfill
steps.purpose: Ensure the zone behind the faulted AGV is correctly cleared so exchange can resume.
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), check whether the AGV behind the faulted AGV backfills into the expected position. If it does not backfill, remove that trailing AGV as well using the same AGV API Controls flow referenced by the manual.
steps.expected_result: Either (a) the AGV behind backfills into the expected position, or (b) the trailing AGV is removed from RMS when it does not backfill.
steps.healthy_condition: Backfill occurs as expected, or the trailing AGV is successfully removed so the zone can be re-established with the correct tote + empty AGV state.
steps.failure_condition: The trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described.

actions.label: Verify backfill behavior
actions.exact_action: Check whether the AGV behind it does not back fill.

actions.label: Remove trailing AGV (if no backfill)

stop_or_escalate_if: Trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described — escalate.

steps.healthy_condition: The affected exchange location shows the newly introduced tote and an empty AGV in the zone (exchange can resume).
steps.failure_condition: The new tote/empty AGV cannot be introduced into the correct zone.

actions.label: Place empty AGV in zone

success_criteria: Faulted AGV is removed from RMS.

healthy_conditions: RMS remains stopped during removal/reconfiguration actions.

Backfill occurs as expected OR trailing AGV is removed when backfill does not occur.
