failure_conditions: Trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described.
New tote and/or empty AGV cannot be introduced into the correct zone.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if the trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described, or if the new tote/empty AGV cannot be introduced into the correct zone.

structured_payload.summary: Perform the required AGV start-up prerequisites (nine empty AGVs: five under the north rack and four under the south rack), start the OptiSweep system 15 minutes before the sort, run the documented start sequence (Reset Metrics → Start System → Close Out/Bag Out), verify the system returns to the "Running" state after Bag Out, and then shut down.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use to start the OptiSweep AGV system for an upcoming sort, ensuring the system is properly prepared (nine empty AGVs) and that the system transitions back to the "Running" state after close out (Bag Out).

steps.title: Verify nine empty AGVs are present (5 north / 4 south)
steps.purpose: Ensure the documented prerequisite for starting the system is met (enough AGVs without totes in the north and south rack zones).
steps.instruction: Verify there are nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack.
steps.expected_result: You confirm five (5) empty AGVs under the north rack and four (4) empty AGVs under the south rack.
steps.healthy_condition: North rack has 5 AGVs without totes and south rack has 4 AGVs without totes.
steps.failure_condition: Fewer than nine empty AGVs are present, or the north/south distribution is not 5 north and 4 south.

actions.label: Check empty AGV counts by rack zone
actions.exact_action: Verify there are nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system—five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the nine empty AGV prerequisite cannot be met (5 under north rack, 4 under south rack), do not proceed until an empty AGV is moved into the missing zone and added to the RMS.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Before starting the system, make sure there are enough AGVs without totes in the system. There should be nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack.

steps.title: Move an empty AGV into the missing zone and add it to RMS (if needed)
steps.purpose: Satisfy the prerequisite when the system is started without nine totes/empty AGVs by moving an empty AGV into the deficient zone and registering it in RMS.
steps.instruction: If fewer than nine empty AGVs are present, move an AGV without a tote into the zone that is missing an empty AGV, then add that AGV to the RMS after moving it.
steps.expected_result: The missing zone now has an empty AGV, and the moved AGV has been added to RMS.
steps.healthy_condition: After adding the moved AGV in RMS, the AGV is successfully registered (per the RMS add screen procedure, the AGV turns blue and its status is verified as "szonestaging").
steps.failure_condition: The missing zone remains without an empty AGV, or the moved AGV does not successfully register in RMS (e.g., does not turn blue / cannot be verified as "szonestaging").

actions.label: Move empty AGV into deficient zone
actions.exact_action: Move an AGV without a tote into the zone that is missing an empty AGV.

actions.label: Add AGV to RMS
actions.exact_action: Make sure to add the AGV to the RMS after moving the AGV.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the nine empty AGV prerequisite cannot be met (5 under north rack, 4 under south rack), do not proceed without moving an empty AGV into the missing zone and adding it to the RMS.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If the system is started without nine totes, an AGV without a tote will need to be moved into the zone that is missing an AGV. Make sure to add the AGV to the RMS after moving the AGV.

content.text: If empty AGVs lose their tasks after an RMS restart, stop RMS, remove and re-add the affected empty AGVs without totes twice, verify each AGV is in the "szonestaging" state on the HMI, press E-stop again when ready, then resume RMS.

structured_payload.title: Recover Empty AGVs That Lost Tasks After RMS Restart (Remove/Re-add AGVs Twice)
structured_payload.summary: If empty AGVs lose their tasks after an RMS restart, stop RMS, remove and re-add the affected empty AGVs without totes twice, verify each AGV is in the "szonestaging" state on the HMI, press E-stop again when ready, then resume RMS.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when empty AGVs have lost their tasks because the RMS was restarted, and the recovery guidance calls for removing and re-adding the AGVs twice and confirming "szonestaging" before resuming RMS.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute the RMS stop/resume and the RMS Tote API Controls remove/re-add cycle, and verify AGV state on the HMI before resuming RMS.
safety_notes: Do not resume RMS until the affected AGVs are confirmed in the "szonestaging" state on the HMI.
access_or_tools_needed: Hospital HMI / lane UI (hospital_hmi) used to reference AGV state

access_required: RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui)
Hospital HMI / lane UI (hospital_hmi)
system_preconditions: The issue condition matches: empty AGVs have lost their tasks because the RMS was restarted.

steps.title: E-stop RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.purpose: Stop RMS before performing the remove/re-add recovery cycle for empty AGVs that lost tasks after an RMS restart.

steps.expected_result: RMS is in an E-stopped state on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS E-stop control is engaged/active on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.failure_condition: RMS is not stopped (E-stop does not engage) or the UI does not reflect an E-stopped state.

actions.label: Press RMS E-stop
actions.exact_action: E-stop RMS.

stop_or_escalate_if: If RMS E-stop cannot be engaged, stop and escalate.

steps.title: Remove and re-add empty AGVs without totes twice using Tote API Controls
steps.purpose: Restore task assignment for empty AGVs that lost tasks after RMS restart by performing the required remove/re-add cycle twice.
steps.instruction: Using the Tote API Controls flow within the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), remove and re-add the affected empty AGVs without totes twice.
steps.expected_result: Each affected empty AGV has been removed and re-added twice via the RMS Tote API Controls flow.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGVs proceed through the expected post-add state progression (next step will verify "szonestaging").
steps.failure_condition: The AGVs do not progress as expected after the remove/re-add cycle, or the remove/re-add operation cannot be completed.

actions.label: Remove/re-add AGVs twice (no totes)
actions.exact_action: Remove and re-add AGVs without totes twice. (See "Tote API Controls" on page 26.)

stop_or_escalate_if: If the remove/re-add cycle cannot be completed twice, stop and escalate.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 5.8.2.3: AGVS LOST TASKS... 2. Remove and re-add AGVs without totes twice. (See "Tote API Controls" on page 26.)

steps.title: Verify AGVs are in "szonestaging" on the HMI
steps.purpose: Ensure the required AGV state is achieved before pressing E-stop again and resuming RMS.
steps.instruction: If the system needs to be restarted, verify on the HMI (hospital_hmi) that the affected AGVs are in the "szonestaging" state by referencing the AGV state/value on the HMI.
steps.expected_result: The affected empty AGVs show AGV status/state value "szonestaging" on the HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV status is "szonestaging" for the affected empty AGVs.
steps.failure_condition: Any affected empty AGV is not in "szonestaging" state.

actions.label: Check AGV state = szonestaging
actions.exact_action: Verify AGV status is "szonestaging". (Reference AGV state on HMI.)

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if AGVs cannot be brought to "szonestaging".

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 5.8.2.3: AGVS LOST TASKS... 3. If the system needs to be restarted, make sure the AGVs are in the "szonestaging" state. (Reference AGV state on the HMI.)

steps.title: Press E-stop again when ready to resume
steps.purpose: Complete the required stop/resume sequence after the AGVs are confirmed in "szonestaging".
steps.instruction: When the affected empty AGVs are confirmed in "szonestaging" on the HMI, press the E-stop again on the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) when ready to resume.
steps.expected_result: The RMS E-stop control is pressed again (as indicated by the RMS / fleet status UI).
steps.healthy_condition: E-stop again action is accepted and the system is ready for RMS resumption.
steps.failure_condition: E-stop again cannot be performed or RMS does not proceed to the resume-ready state.

actions.label: Press E-stop again
actions.exact_action: Press the E-stop again when ready to resume.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not resume RMS until AGVs are confirmed in "szonestaging" state on the HMI.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 5.8.2.3: AGVS LOST TASKS... 4. Press the E-stop again when ready to resume.

steps.title: Resume RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.purpose: Restart RMS operations after the recovery cycle and state verification.
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), resume RMS.
steps.expected_result: RMS resumes/starts successfully on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS is resumed and the affected empty AGVs are no longer in the lost-task condition.
steps.failure_condition: Lost-task condition persists after resuming RMS.

actions.label: Resume RMS
actions.exact_action: Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.)

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the lost-task condition persists after the twice remove/re-add process.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 5.8.2.3: AGVS LOST TASKS... 5. Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.)

success_criteria: RMS is resumed on the RMS / fleet status UI.
Affected empty AGVs are no longer in the lost-task condition after the remove/re-add cycle and "szonestaging" verification.
healthy_conditions: Affected empty AGVs show AGV status/state value "szonestaging" on the HMI.
RMS is resumed/started on the RMS / fleet status UI.
failure_conditions: Any affected empty AGV cannot be brought to "szonestaging".
Lost-task condition persists after the twice remove/re-add process and RMS resumption.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if AGVs cannot be brought to "szonestaging" or if the lost-task condition persists after the twice remove/re-add process.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: 5.8.2.3: AGVS LOST TASKS... 1. E-stop RMS. 2. Remove and re-add AGVs without totes twice. 3. If the system needs to be restarted, make sure the AGVs are in the "szonestaging" state. 4. Press the E-stop again when ready to resume. 5. Resume RMS. NOTE: The best practice is to shut down and restart to ensure everything is in sync.

content.text: When RMS shows an AGV “Bump” fault with Exception Code 21057 or 21060, stop RMS, remove the obstruction that caused the bump/obstacle trigger, hold the AGV RESET button for two seconds to clear the fault, press E-stop again, then resume RMS. structured_payload.title: Recover an AGV “BUMP” fault (Exception Codes 21057/21060) using RMS
structured_payload.summary: When RMS shows an AGV “Bump” fault with Exception Code 21057 or 21060, stop RMS, remove the obstruction that caused the bump/obstacle trigger, hold the AGV RESET button for two seconds to clear the fault, press E-stop again, then resume RMS. Verify the Exception Code is cleared on the RMS “Bump” Fault Screen before resuming normal operation.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this procedure when the RMS interface displays an AGV “Bump” fault and the Exception Code shown is 21057 or 21060, indicating a collision bar trigger or obstacle-avoidance trigger that requires RMS-side fault recovery.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for physical obstruction removal when the bump/obstacle trigger is caused by an on-grid obstruction; the obstruction must be physically cleared before attempting RESET.
Do not proceed to resume RMS if the Exception Code remains after the two-second AGV RESET attempt.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute RMS-side recovery actions (E-stop RMS, use AGV RESET for two seconds, press E-stop again, resume RMS) and verify the Exception Code is cleared on the RMS “Bump” Fault Screen.
safety_notes: This procedure includes E-stopping RMS (not physical E-stop).
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to remove the obstruction on the grid

content.text: Replace the flat-flex cable (FFC) connected to the A-axis PCA on a tipper station that has been LOTOed. Use the correct replacement part and ensure the correct left/right ClearLink controller hardware is installed (left/right are not interchangeable due to different IP addresses). The procedure removes the two FFC clamps (four M3 socket-head screws), unplugs/replugs the FFC, then reinstalls the clamps and the station side panel (nine self-tapping securing screws).

steps.title: Open cross bars and remove the old cable carrier

steps.instruction: Open all the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier, and remove it from the FFC and air line. You may have to snap one end of the cable carrier off to fully remove it.
steps.expected_result: Old cable carrier is removed from the FFC and air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Cross bars are fully opened and carrier comes free without pulling on the FFC or air line.
steps.failure_condition: Carrier cannot be removed because cross bars are not fully opened or it is still attached.

actions.label: Open cross bars
actions.exact_action: Open all the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier

actions.label: Remove carrier
actions.exact_action: remove it from the FFC and air line. You may have to snap one end of the cable carrier off to fully remove it.

source_evidence.quote: 7. Open all the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier, and remove it from the FFC and air line. You may have to snap one end of the cable carrier off to fully remove it.

steps.title: Position the new cable carrier with dividers against the air line
steps.purpose: Set the new carrier in the correct orientation and clearance before snapping it closed.
steps.instruction: Open all the cross bars on the new cable carrier and probably one end. Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.
steps.expected_result: New carrier is positioned roughly in place with internal dividers positioned against the air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Dividers are positioned all the way to one side against the air line before snapping cross bars closed.
steps.failure_condition: Dividers are not positioned against the air line, increasing risk of divider pressing on the FFC.

actions.label: Open new carrier cross bars
actions.exact_action: Open all the cross bars on the new cable carrier and probably one end.

actions.label: Position dividers against air line
actions.exact_action: Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.

source_evidence.quote: 8. Open all the cross bars on the new cable carrier and probably one end. 9. Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.

steps.title: Snap cross bars closed ensuring dividers do not press on the FFC
steps.purpose: Lock the carrier in place while preserving FFC clearance.
steps.instruction: “Snap” all the cross bars closed, ensuring none of the dividers are pressing on the FFC; snap the end back on if necessary.
steps.expected_result: All cross bars are snapped closed and dividers are not pressing on the FFC.
steps.healthy_condition: No divider contact/pressure on the FFC is visible; carrier ends are fully snapped in place.
steps.failure_condition: Any divider is pressing on the FFC.

actions.label: Snap cross bars closed
actions.exact_action: “Snap” all the cross bars closed ensuring none of the dividers are pressing on the FFC and snap the end back on if necessary.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment/clearance if dividers are pressing on the FFC.

source_evidence.quote: 10. “Snap” all the cross bars closed ensuring none of the dividers are pressing on the FFC and snap the end back on if necessary.

steps.title: Mount both ends of the cable carrier with M3 flat-head screws
steps.purpose: Secure the carrier ends to the station structure.
steps.instruction: Mount both ends using four M3 flat-head screws.
steps.expected_result: Both ends are mounted with four M3 flat-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: All specified screws are installed at both ends and the carrier is firmly secured.
steps.failure_condition: Any end is missing screws or carrier is loose.

actions.label: Install mounting screws
actions.exact_action: Mount both ends using four M3 flat-head.

source_evidence.quote: 11. Mount both ends using four M3 flat-head.

steps.title: Attach FFC clamps using M3 socket-head screws aligned to marks
steps.purpose: Restore correct FFC clamp alignment and secure the FFC to the carrier ends.
steps.instruction: Attach the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws at both cable carrier ends; ensure the FFC clamps align with the marks from Step 1.
steps.expected_result: FFC clamps are secured at both ends and aligned to the previously applied marks.
steps.healthy_condition: Clamp positions match the Step 1 marks; clamps are seated and secured with M3 socket-head screws.
steps.failure_condition: Clamp alignment does not match the marks (risk of FFC misalignment).

actions.label: Install FFC clamp screws
actions.exact_action: Attach the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws at both cable carrier ends; ensure the FFC clamps align with the marks from Step 1.

source_evidence.quote: 12. Attach the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws at both cable carrier ends. Ensure the FFC clamps still align with the marks from Step 1.

steps.title: Wire-tie the air line in the cable carrier using marks
steps.purpose: Restore air line routing and secure it within the carrier.
steps.instruction: Position the air line in the cable carrier using the marks from Step 1 and wire tie it in place.
steps.expected_result: Air line is positioned according to Step 1 marks and secured with wire ties.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line routing matches the marks and is firmly wire-tied without slack or strain.
steps.failure_condition: Air line is mispositioned relative to marks or not secured.

actions.label: Wire-tie air line
actions.exact_action: Position the air line in the cable carrier using the marks from Step 1 and wire tie in place.

source_evidence.quote: 13. Position the air line in the cable carrier using the marks from Step 1 and wire tie in place.

steps.title: Inspect cable carrier seating, clearance, and joint uniformity
steps.purpose: Confirm the carrier is correctly installed before restarting.
steps.instruction: Inspect the cable carrier: verify all cross bars are closed, the dividers are not pressing on the FFC, and all the cable carrier joints are fully seated. The cable carrier should look very uniform end to end.
steps.expected_result: Cross bars are closed; dividers are not pressing on the FFC; joints are fully seated; carrier appears uniform end-to-end.
steps.healthy_condition: Visual inspection shows uniform end-to-end appearance with no divider pressure on the FFC and fully seated joints.
steps.failure_condition: Any cross bar is not closed, dividers press on the FFC, or joints are not fully seated (non-uniform appearance).

actions.label: Visual inspection
actions.exact_action: Inspect the cable carrier to ensure all the cross bars are closed, the dividers are not pressing on the FFC, and all the cable carrier joints are fully seated.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment/clearance if dividers are pressing on the FFC or if cable carrier joints do not appear fully seated/uniform end-to-end.

source_evidence.quote: 14. Inspect the cable carrier to ensure all the cross bars are closed, the dividers are not pressing on the FFC, and all the cable carrier joints are fully seated. The cable carrier will look uniform end to end.

steps.title: Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels (if necessary)
steps.purpose: Restore station enclosure after reassembly.
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
steps.expected_result: Top and/or bottom side panels are reinstalled as required.
steps.healthy_condition: Panels are installed and the station is re-closed without leaving access panels open.
steps.failure_condition: Panels not reinstalled when required, leaving components exposed.

actions.label: Reinstall panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

source_evidence.quote: 15. Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.purpose: Bring the system back to operational state after mechanical replacement.
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.expected_result: Operator station restarts successfully.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station restart completes without failure and system proceeds to normal operation.
steps.failure_condition: Operator station does not restart after reassembly.

actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station does not restart after reassembly, escalate to the appropriate support process (manual references “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).

source_evidence.quote: 16. Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

content.text: Safely stop the OptiSweep tipper cycle from the operator station HMI, lock out the tipper at the station e-panel, and disconnect the gripper hardware (valve cover, supply air line, four M8 connectors, and the A-axis cable carrier routed through the grommet) to prepare for gripper replacement.

structured_payload.title: Remove OptiSweep Gripper at the Operator Station (LOTO + Disconnect Valve/Air/Cables)
structured_payload.summary: Safely stop the OptiSweep tipper cycle from the operator station HMI, lock out the tipper at the station e-panel, and disconnect the gripper hardware (valve cover, supply air line, four M8 connectors, and the A-axis cable carrier routed through the grommet) to prepare for gripper replacement.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when performing OptiSweep gripper replacement removal at the operator station and you must stop the cycle, LOTO the tipper, and disconnect the gripper’s valve/air/electrical connections and A-axis cable carrier.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Executes HMI cycle stop/jog positioning, performs station e-panel LOTO, and performs the physical disconnection/removal steps for the gripper hardware.
safety_notes: CAUTION HEAVY EQUIPMENT: Components may be heavy. Use caution when lifting. Failure to follow these instructions can result in injury or equipment damage.
access_or_tools_needed: Axis buttons for the corresponding tipper
Tools: 2.5-mm hex wrench, 3-mm hex wrench, 5-mm hex wrench, 6-mm hex wrench, Loctite® (as listed)
Replacement part: gripper (for the overall replacement task)

access_required: Operator station HMI access
Station e-panel access for LOTO

steps.title: Navigate to Visu_MCP_Dual on the operator station HMI
steps.purpose: Open the operator station screen that provides cycle stop and manual jog controls for positioning the gripper.
steps.instruction: At the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
steps.expected_result: The "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen is displayed and ready for control inputs.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the controls needed to stop the cycle and manually jog the tipper (CYCLE STOP and JOG).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen or cannot locate the CYCLE STOP/JOG controls.

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: At the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.

steps.title: Stop the cycle and enable manual tipper control
steps.purpose: Bring the system to a stopped state and switch to manual control for positioning the gripper.
steps.instruction: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the cycle, then press JOG to manually control the tipper.
steps.expected_result: The cycle is stopped and manual control is enabled via JOG.
steps.healthy_condition: The tipper is under manual control (JOG active) and the cycle is not running.
steps.failure_condition: The cycle does not stop or manual control cannot be enabled.

actions.label: Cycle stop
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the cycle

actions.label: Enable jog
actions.exact_action: press JOG to manually control the tipper

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the cycle, then press JOG to manually control the tipper.

steps.title: Move the gripper to the desired location using axis buttons
steps.purpose: Position the gripper so it can be safely disconnected and removed.
steps.instruction: Use the axis buttons for the corresponding tipper to move the gripper to the desired location.
steps.expected_result: The gripper is positioned at the desired location using the axis buttons.
steps.healthy_condition: The gripper moves as commanded and reaches the intended position for the removal/disconnection steps.
steps.failure_condition: The gripper does not move as expected or cannot be positioned to the required location.

actions.label: Move gripper
actions.exact_action: Use the axis buttons for the corresponding tipper to move the gripper to the desired location

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Use the axis buttons for the corresponding tipper to move the gripper to the desired location.

steps.title: Support carriages if gripper is moved from home position
steps.purpose: Prevent carriage drop by supporting them with screws when the gripper is not at its home position.
steps.instruction: If the gripper is moved from its home position, thread screws into the threaded holes in the column to support the carriages between the pair or holes.
steps.expected_result: Screws are threaded into the column threaded holes to support the carriages between the pair or holes.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are supported by the threaded screws (no unsupported drop condition).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot support the carriages with screws in the threaded holes, or support is incomplete.

actions.label: Thread support screws
actions.exact_action: thread screws into the threaded holes in the column to support the carriages between the pair or holes

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot support the carriages while preparing for gripper removal.

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: NOTE: If the gripper is moved from its home position, thread screws into the threaded holes in the column to support the carriages between the pair or holes.

steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is applied at the station e-panel for the tipper you are working on.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot perform LOTO safely at the station e-panel.

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: LOTO the tipper at the station e-panel (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Verify correct gripper selection (left vs right)
steps.purpose: Ensure you disconnect the correct gripper hardware before removing valve cover, air line, and connectors.
steps.instruction: Verify the correct gripper has been selected (i.e., left gripper or right gripper).
steps.expected_result: You confirm whether the left or right gripper is selected for the removal/disconnection work.
steps.healthy_condition: The selected gripper matches the physical gripper you are about to disconnect.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm left vs right gripper selection before disconnecting hardware.

actions.label: Confirm left/right selection
actions.exact_action: Verify the correct gripper has been selected (i.e., left gripper or right gripper)

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Verify the correct gripper has been selected (i.e., left gripper or right gripper).

steps.title: Remove valve cover (four M4x50 socket-head screws)
steps.purpose: Expose the valve/gripper assembly connections for subsequent disconnection steps.
steps.instruction: Remove the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws from the valve cover, then remove the valve cover.
steps.expected_result: The valve cover is removed after removing the four M4x50 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Valve cover is fully detached and removed; screws are removed from the cover.
steps.failure_condition: Valve cover cannot be removed or screws are not fully removed.

actions.label: Remove valve cover screws

actions.label: Remove valve cover
actions.exact_action: Remove the valve cover

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Remove the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws from the valve cover. Remove the valve cover.

steps.title: Disconnect all four M8 connectors
steps.purpose: Disconnect electrical connections to the gripper/valve assembly before removing or further disconnecting air and cable components.
steps.instruction: Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors.
steps.expected_result: All four M8 connectors are disconnected from the valve/gripper assembly.
steps.healthy_condition: No M8 connectors remain connected to the gripper/valve assembly.
steps.failure_condition: Any M8 connector remains connected or cannot be disconnected.

actions.label: Disconnect M8 connectors
actions.exact_action: Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors.

steps.title: Disconnect the supply air line on top of the valve
steps.purpose: Remove pneumatic connection so the gripper can be disconnected and removed safely.
steps.instruction: Disconnect the supply air line on the top of the valve.
steps.expected_result: The supply air line is disconnected from the top of the valve.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line is disconnected at the valve connection point.
steps.failure_condition: Air line cannot be disconnected or remains attached.

actions.label: Disconnect air line
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the supply air line on the top of the valve

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Disconnect the supply air line on the top of the valve.

steps.title: Plug fitting and cap air line to prevent debris entry
steps.purpose: Prevent debris from entering the air line/fitting after disconnection.
steps.instruction: Plug the fitting and cap the air line to prevent debris from entering either; if plugs/caps are not available, use tape to protect both.
steps.expected_result: The fitting is plugged and the air line is capped (or protected with tape if plugs/caps are unavailable).
steps.healthy_condition: Both ends are protected against debris entry.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot apply plugs/caps or tape protection to both the fitting and air line.

actions.label: Protect air line ends
actions.exact_action: Plug the fitting and cap the air line... If plugs and caps are not available, use tape to protect both.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if plugs/caps (or tape protection) cannot be applied to prevent debris entering the air line/fitting.

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Plug the fitting and cap the air line to prevent debris from entering either. If plugs and caps are not available, use tape to protect both.

steps.title: Feed capped air line through the grommet
steps.purpose: Route the protected air line through the grommet to clear the assembly for cable routing/disconnection.
steps.instruction: Feed the capped air line through the grommet.
steps.expected_result: The capped air line is routed through the grommet.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line passes through the grommet without obstruction and remains capped/plugged.
steps.failure_condition: Air line cannot be fed through the grommet or becomes unprotected.

actions.label: Route air line

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Feed the capped air line through the grommet.

steps.purpose: Clear the cable routing so the M8 connectors and A-axis cable carrier can be detached.

steps.expected_result: The jacketed part of the cable is pulled out of the grommet.
steps.healthy_condition: Cable jacket is free from the grommet and can be routed/handled for the next steps.
steps.failure_condition: Cable cannot be pulled out or is snagged such that it cannot be safely routed.

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Pull the jacketed part of the cable out of the grommet.

steps.purpose: Route the disconnected electrical connectors through the grommet to free the gripper assembly.
steps.instruction: Feed all of the M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time.
steps.expected_result: All four M8 connectors are routed through the grommet.
steps.healthy_condition: Each M8 connector passes through the grommet without damage and is fully free of the grommet.
steps.failure_condition: Any M8 connector cannot be fed through the grommet or is damaged during routing.

actions.label: Route M8 connectors

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Feed all of the M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time.

steps.purpose: Restore the valve cover after disconnecting air/electrical and before proceeding to gripper-to-gearbox fastener removal.

steps.healthy_condition: Valve cover is seated and all four screws are installed.

steps.title: Remove gripper-to-gearbox attachment screws (M6x20) and support counter-balance
steps.purpose: Detach the gripper from the gearbox while preventing imbalance by supporting the counter-balance.
steps.instruction: Remove the 10 M6x20 socket-head screws attaching the gripper to the gearbox (suggested: fully remove nine (9) screws). Ensure the counter-balance is supported.
steps.expected_result: The gripper-to-gearbox attachment screws are removed (with the suggested approach of fully removing nine), and the counter-balance is supported.
steps.healthy_condition: Counter-balance remains supported during screw removal; gripper attachment is loosened as intended.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance cannot be supported while removing the gripper-to-gearbox screws.

actions.label: Remove M6x20 screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the 10 M6x20 socket-head screws attaching the gripper to the gearbox (suggested: fully remove nine (9) screws). Ensure the counter-balance is supported.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the counter-balance cannot be supported while removing the gripper-to-gearbox screws.

source_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Remove the 10 M6x20 socket-head screws attaching the gripper to the gearbox. a. It is suggested to fully remove nine (9) of the screws. b. Ensure the counter-balance is supported.

success_criteria: Cycle is stopped and tipper is LOTO’d.
Gripper is positioned as required.
Valve cover is removed (then reinstalled per procedure).
Four M8 connectors are disconnected.
Supply air line is disconnected and protected (plugged/capped or taped).
Air line and cable are routed through the grommet.
A-axis cable carrier is detached by removing two M3x8 screws (saved).
Gripper-to-gearbox attachment screws (M6x20) are removed with counter-balance supported.
healthy_conditions: LOTO is applied at the station e-panel for the tipper being serviced.
Correct left vs right gripper selection is confirmed before disconnecting hardware.
Air line fitting and air line are protected to prevent debris entry.
Counter-balance is supported during M6x20 screw removal.
failure_conditions: Cannot confirm correct gripper selection (left vs right) before disconnecting hardware.
Counter-balance cannot be supported while removing gripper-to-gearbox screws.
Cannot apply plugs/caps (or tape protection) to prevent debris entering the air line/fitting.
Valve cover cannot be removed/reinstalled as specified (screws not removed/installed).
Any M8 connector cannot be disconnected or routed through the grommet.
escalation_guidance: If you cannot confirm correct gripper selection (left vs right) before disconnecting hardware, stop work and escalate.
If you cannot support the counter-balance while removing the gripper-to-gearbox screws, stop work and escalate.
If plugs/caps (or tape protection) cannot be applied to prevent debris entering the air line/fitting, stop work and escalate.
If you cannot perform LOTO safely at the station e-panel, stop work and escalate.

content.text: Prepare a tipper for gripper removal by stopping the current cycle, enabling manual jogging on the operator station HMI (Visu_MCP_Dual), positioning the gripper at the specified location, optionally supporting the carriages if the gripper is moved off home, and performing LOTO at the station e-panel. Confirm the correct gripper selection (left vs right) before proceeding.

structured_payload.title: Remove and Support Gripper for a Tipper Using Visu_MCP_Dual (Cycle Stop + Jog) and LOTO
structured_payload.summary: Prepare a tipper for gripper removal by stopping the current cycle, enabling manual jogging on the operator station HMI (Visu_MCP_Dual), positioning the gripper at the specified location, optionally supporting the carriages if the gripper is moved off home, and performing LOTO at the station e-panel. Confirm the correct gripper selection (left vs right) before proceeding.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when you must remove a tipper gripper and need to stop the cycle, jog the tipper/gripper to the required location, mechanically support the carriages if the gripper is moved from home, and apply LOTO at the station e-panel before removal.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a general tipper fault troubleshooting guide; it is specifically for gripper removal preparation (stop/jog/LOTO/left-right verification).

safety_notes: Caution: Components may be heavy. Use caution when lifting (gripper replacement section includes this caution).

steps.title: Stop the cycle and enable manual jogging
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper cycle is stopped and manual control is enabled so the gripper can be positioned safely.
steps.instruction: Press "CYCLE STOP" to stop the cycle, then press "JOG" to manually control the tipper.

steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before any mechanical removal work.
steps.instruction: Apply lockout/tagout to the tipper (manual references “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on page 2).
steps.expected_result: The tipper is LOTOed and ready for mechanical work.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place before removing any side panel or fasteners.
steps.failure_condition: Mechanical removal begins without LOTO.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

source_evidence.quote: 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove station side panel if necessary to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area as needed for the idler pulley assembly removal.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed and the motor access area is available.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine self-tapping securing screws are removed and the side panel is off without forcing.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not fully secured/removed (e.g., screws left in place) or panel removal is attempted without removing the specified screws.

actions.label: Check if side panel removal is needed
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

source_evidence.quote: 2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Position A-axis and counterbalance between actuator base threaded holes
steps.purpose: Set the A-axis/counterbalance carriages to the correct location so they can be secured and will not drop when belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base: there are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are located between the specified threaded holes on their respective rails.
steps.failure_condition: Carriages are not between the threaded holes (mispositioned), increasing risk of dropping when tension is released.

actions.label: Manually position carriages
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

source_evidence.quote: 3. Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Mechanically secure the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop once belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages, preventing drop when belt tension is released.
steps.healthy_condition: Both carriages are secured by the M6 socket-head screws below them.
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws are not installed below both carriages before belt tension is released.

actions.label: Install M6 securing screws
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance is not held securely by the threaded M6 socket-head screws before loosening belt tension (risk of dropping).

source_evidence.quote: 3. ... Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

steps.title: Remove belt clamps by removing six M6x20 countersunk screws
steps.purpose: Free the carriages from the belt so belt tension can be released and the idler pulley assembly can be removed.
steps.instruction: Remove the belt clamps by removing the six (6) M6x20 countersunk screws with a 5-mm hex wrench from each clamp to free the carriages from the belt.
steps.expected_result: Belt clamps are removed and carriages are free from the belt.
steps.healthy_condition: All six M6x20 countersunk screws per clamp are removed and the clamp(s) are off without binding the belt.
steps.failure_condition: Any clamp fasteners remain installed, preventing carriage/belt separation.

actions.label: Remove belt clamp screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the belt clamps by removing the six (6) M6x20 countersunk screws with a 5-mm hex wrench from each clamp to free the carriages from the belt.

source_evidence.quote: 4. Remove the belt clamps by removing the six (6) M6x20 countersunk screws with a 5-mm hex wrench from each clamp to free the carriages from the belt.

steps.title: Release belt tension by loosening two M6x35 socket-head screws
steps.purpose: Remove tension from the belt so the idler pulley assembly can be unfastened and slid out.
steps.instruction: Release belt tension by loosening the two (2) M6x35 socket-head screws on the bottom side of the assembly.
steps.expected_result: Belt tension is released after loosening the two M6x35 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: After loosening, the belt is no longer under tension (mechanically slackened) while the A-axis/counterbalance remains secured by the M6 screws.
steps.failure_condition: Belt tension is released without the A-axis/counterbalance being secured (risk of dropping).

actions.label: Loosen tensioning screws
actions.exact_action: Release belt tension by loosening the two (2) M6x35 socket-head screws on the bottom side of the assembly.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance is not held securely by the threaded M6 socket-head screws before loosening belt tension (risk of dropping).

source_evidence.quote: 5. Release belt tension by loosening the two (2) M6x35 socket-head screws on the bottom side of the assembly.

steps.title: Remove idler pulley assembly and slide it out of the column
steps.purpose: Unfasten the idler pulley assembly and remove it from the tipper column for replacement.
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) M8x25 socket-head screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place, then slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column. If needed, transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws from the removed idler pulley assembly to the new assembly.
steps.expected_result: The two M8x25 screws are removed and the idler pulley assembly slides out of the column; if required, M6x35 tensioning screws are transferred to the new assembly.
steps.healthy_condition: Idler pulley assembly is fully removed with no remaining fasteners; tensioning screws are available on the new assembly if the manual note applies.
steps.failure_condition: Idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 socket-head screws (possible remaining fasteners or misalignment).

actions.label: Remove mounting screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) M8x25 socket-head screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place

actions.label: Slide assembly out
actions.exact_action: then slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column.

actions.label: Transfer tensioning screws if needed
actions.exact_action: NOTE: Transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws from the removed idler pulley assembly to the new assembly if needed.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 socket-head screws (possible remaining fasteners or misalignment).

source_evidence.quote: 6. Remove the two (2) M8x25 socket-head screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place and slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column. NOTE: Transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws from the removed idler pulley assembly to the new assembly if needed.

success_criteria: Tipper remains LOTOed throughout the mechanical removal steps.
A-axis and counterbalance are secured with M6 socket-head screws before belt tension is released.
Belt clamps are removed (six M6x20 countersunk screws per clamp) and belt tension is released (two M6x35 socket-head screws loosened).
Idler pulley assembly is unfastened (two M8x25 socket-head screws removed) and slid out of the column.
If required, M6x35 tensioning screws are transferred to the new idler pulley assembly.
healthy_conditions: Carriages are positioned between the actuator base threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
M6 socket-head screws are installed below both carriages.
Belt clamps are removed and belt tension is released without the A-axis/counterbalance dropping.
Idler pulley assembly slides out after removing the two M8x25 screws.
failure_conditions: A-axis/counterbalance is not held securely by the threaded M6 socket-head screws before loosening belt tension.
Idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 socket-head screws.
escalation_guidance: If the A-axis/counterbalance is not secured before belt tension release, stop and escalate due to risk of dropping.
If the idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 screws, stop and escalate for inspection of remaining fasteners or misalignment.

content.text: Replace/install the Tip or A-Axis cable by routing it correctly around the gearbox and into the cable carrier, securing it, routing all required M8 connectors through the grommet, connecting the labeled Valve/tote detect/LONG/SHORT gripper sensors, installing the valve cover without pinching wires, reinstalling side panels if needed, and restarting the operator station.

structured_payload.title: Install Tip or A-Axis Cable (A-axis PCA to cable carrier/grommet and sensor/valve M8 connectors)
structured_payload.summary: Replace/install the Tip or A-Axis cable by routing it correctly around the gearbox and into the cable carrier, securing it, routing all required M8 connectors through the grommet, connecting the labeled Valve/tote detect/LONG/SHORT gripper sensors, installing the valve cover without pinching wires, reinstalling side panels if needed, and restarting the operator station.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when the Tip or A-Axis cable needs replacement/installation and you must ensure correct cable routing, grommet use, labeled M8 connector connections (Valve, tote detect, LONG/SHORT gripper sensors), valve cover installation without pinching wires, and a successful operator station restart.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the physical installation steps (routing, securing, connector installation, valve cover and side panel reassembly) and restart the operator station.
safety_notes: The source references LOTO in the surrounding Tip or A-Axis cable section (7.3.15.1 REMOVAL) and includes PPE/tooling context for the Tip or A-Axis cable work.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the A-axis PCA, gearbox area, cable carrier, cross bars, grommet, valve, tote detect sensor, LONG/SHORT gripper sensors, and valve cover

access_required: Physical access to the tipper/operator station area containing the A-axis PCA, gearbox, cable carrier, grommet, sensors, and valve cover
system_preconditions: Tipper/operator station is in a safe state for maintenance work (source context references LOTO for this cable procedure section)
external_references: Starting The Operator Station (referenced by the source as the restart procedure on page 66)

steps.title: Plug new cable into A-axis PCA and route around gearbox into cable carrier
steps.purpose: Establish correct electrical connection at the A-axis PCA and ensure the cable follows the required routing path around the gearbox and into the cable carrier.
steps.instruction: Plug the new Tip or A-Axis cable into the A-axis PCA, then route the cable around the gearbox and into and around the cable carrier.
steps.expected_result: The cable is plugged into the A-axis PCA and physically routed around the gearbox and into/around the cable carrier along the intended path.
steps.healthy_condition: Cable routing matches the installation diagram: cable passes around the gearbox and into/around the cable carrier without being misrouted.
steps.failure_condition: Cable is routed incorrectly around the gearbox/cable carrier or not properly seated at the A-axis PCA.

actions.exact_action: Plug the new cable into the A-axis PCA and route the cable around the gearbox and into and around the cable carrier.

steps.title: Close cross bars with dividers between cable and air line
steps.purpose: Prevent cable/air-line interference by ensuring the cable is separated from the air line using the dividers when the cross bars are closed.
steps.instruction: Close all the cross bars, ensuring the dividers are positioned between the cable and the air line.
steps.expected_result: All cross bars are closed and the dividers are between the cable and the air line.

steps.title: Align cable markings and wire-tie in place (both cable carrier ends and A-axis carriage tie point)

content.text: Use the operator station HMI jogging screen (Visu_Dual_MCP) to stop the automatic tipping cycle and manually move the tipper axes (Z1/A1 for left, Z2/A2 for right) using the +/− controls in Manual Mode.

structured_payload.title: Manually Jog the Tipper End Effector Using Operator Station HMI (Visu_Dual_MCP)
structured_payload.summary: Use the operator station HMI jogging screen (Visu_Dual_MCP) to stop the automatic tipping cycle and manually move the tipper axes (Z1/A1 for left, Z2/A2 for right) using the +/− controls in Manual Mode.
structured_payload.when_to_use: When you need to move the tipper end effector into a desired maintenance position by manually jogging the left and/or right tipper axes from the operator station HMI (Visu_Dual_MCP).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Navigate the operator station HMI to Visu_Dual_MCP, stop the automatic tipping cycle, enter jogging/manual mode, and jog the selected axes using the on-screen +/− controls while avoiding hard stops.
safety_notes: Stop jogging before the axis reaches a hard stop; pushing an axis to a hard stop registers a fault.
access_or_tools_needed: HMI controls: CYCLE STOP, JOG, axis +/− buttons (Z1, Z2, A1, A2)

access_required: Operator station HMI access
system_preconditions: Operator station HMI is available and you can navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).

visual_references.description: Visu_Dual_MCP jogging screen showing Manual Mode and the Z1/Z2/A1/A2 axis +/− controls.
Operator station main screen showing the CYCLE STOP button.

steps.purpose: Open the operator station HMI screen that provides the CYCLE STOP and JOG controls for tipper jogging.
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).
steps.expected_result: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen is displayed and you can access the CYCLE STOP and JOG controls.
steps.healthy_condition: You are on the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) with the tipper operator controls visible.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) or the CYCLE STOP/JOG controls are not available.

steps.instruction: Press "CYCLE STOP" to stop the automatic tipping cycle.

steps.healthy_condition: The operator station is in a state where you can proceed to press JOG to open the jogging screen.
steps.failure_condition: The automatic tipping cycle does not stop (you cannot proceed to jogging as expected).

actions.label: Press CYCLE STOP

steps.failure_condition: The jogging screen does not open or Manual Mode is not indicated.

steps.expected_result: Manual Mode is shown and the axis +/− controls for Z1, Z2, A1, and A2 are visible.

steps.title: Jog the left tipper axes (Z1/A1) or right tipper axes (Z2/A2) using +/−
steps.purpose: Move the tipper end effector into the desired maintenance position by jogging the correct axes.
steps.instruction: Select the axis you want to move and use the "−" and "+" buttons to move it: Z1 (vertical movement) and A1 (rotate gripper) move the left tipper; Z2 and A2 move the right tipper.
steps.expected_result: The selected axis responds to the jog command while Manual Mode is active.
steps.healthy_condition: Jogging causes the intended axis motion for the selected tipper (left via Z1/A1, right via Z2/A2).
steps.failure_condition: The axis does not respond to jog commands or the wrong tipper side moves relative to the axis selection.

actions.label: Select axis and jog with +/−
actions.exact_action: Select the axis you want to move and use the − and + buttons to move the axis.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Z1 AXIS (vertical movement) and A1 AXIS (rotate the gripper) buttons move the left tipper; the Z2 AXIS and A2 AXIS buttons move the right tipper.

steps.title: Use correct +/− motion behavior for Z and A axes
steps.purpose: Ensure the axis moves in the intended direction to reach the maintenance position safely.
steps.instruction: Use the +/− behavior as documented: "+" moves the Z-axis up and rotates the A-axis toward the operator; "−" moves the Z-axis down and rotates the A-axis away from the operator.
steps.expected_result: Pressing "+" produces Z up + A toward operator motion; pressing "−" produces Z down + A away motion.
steps.healthy_condition: Axis motion direction matches the documented +/− behavior.
steps.failure_condition: Axis motion direction is opposite of the documented behavior or does not match the selected axis.

actions.label: Jog with correct +/− direction
actions.exact_action: The + button moves the Z-axis up and rotates the A-axis towards the operator. The − button moves the Z-axis down and rotates the A-axis away from the operator.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: a. The + button moves the Z-axis up and rotates the A-axis towards the operator. b. The − button moves the Z-axis down and rotates the A-axis away from the operator.

steps.title: Avoid hard stops; stop jogging before the axis reaches a hard stop
steps.purpose: Prevent the axis from registering a fault due to contact with a hard stop.
steps.instruction: Stop jogging before the axis reaches a hard stop. Do not push the axis into the hard stop.
steps.expected_result: No hard-stop fault is registered while jogging.
steps.healthy_condition: You can position the end effector without triggering a fault indication.
steps.failure_condition: The axis registers a fault after being pushed to a hard stop.

actions.label: Monitor for hard-stop fault indication
actions.exact_action: If you push the axis until it hits a hard stop, the axis will register a fault.

stop_or_escalate_if: If an axis is driven into a hard stop and the axis registers a fault, stop further jogging and escalate to maintenance/support for the fault condition.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If you push the axis until it hits a hard stop, the axis will register a fault.

failure_conditions: Axis registers a fault after being pushed to a hard stop.
escalation_guidance: If an axis is driven into a hard stop and the axis registers a fault, stop further jogging and escalate to maintenance/support for the fault condition.

structured_payload.title: Determine Tipper/Station Status From Operator Station Stacklights
structured_payload.summary: Use the operator station stacklight color/flash/horn pattern to identify the current status of the corresponding tipper and station, including RMS error, E-stop, tipping state, and bagout/surepost indications.
structured_payload.when_to_use: When you need to determine the current documented status of a tipper/station from the operator station stacklights (solid vs flashing colors, and horn alarm pattern when present).
not_for: Do not use this procedure to clear or reset E-stop or RMS error conditions.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Physically observe the operator station stacklights and interpret the solid/flashing color (and horn alarm pattern when present) into the documented tipper/station status.
safety_notes: If the observed stacklight pattern indicates E-stop activated (Solid Red), escalate immediately and do not attempt to clear remotely from this procedure.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the operator station stacklights
Ability to observe stacklight color(s), solid vs flashing, and horn alarm pattern (long vs intermittent) when present

access_required: Physical access to the operator station stacklights

visual_references.description: Stacklight state meanings (solid/flashing colors and RMS error/fault/AGV presence) used to interpret station status.

Operator station HMI Manual Control screen showing LAMP TEST behavior (audible alarm and stacklight flashing red) and tipper disable/fault reset controls for context while interpreting stacklight signals.
HMI context for Surepost tote indication (stacklight flashes white) and operator station controls (Surepost LEFT/RIGHT).

steps.title: Go to the affected operator station
steps.purpose: Ensure you are observing the correct stacklights for the tipper/station in question.
steps.instruction: Walk to the operator station for the affected tipper/station and position yourself so you can clearly see both stacklights.
steps.expected_result: You can visually identify both stacklights at the operator station for the affected tipper/station.
steps.healthy_condition: Both stacklights are visible and you can distinguish solid vs flashing behavior.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot clearly see one or both stacklights (blocked view, distance, or unclear flashing).

actions.label: Visually confirm stacklight visibility
actions.exact_action: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

steps.title: Observe both stacklights and record solid vs flashing colors
steps.purpose: Capture the observable stacklight pattern that maps to the documented tipper/station status.
steps.instruction: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).
steps.expected_result: You have identified each stacklight’s state (solid/flashing) and color(s).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight colors and flashing behavior are unambiguous (e.g., solid blue vs flashing green, etc.).
steps.failure_condition: The stacklight pattern is unclear (e.g., intermittent visibility) or does not allow confident identification of solid vs flashing and color(s).

actions.label: Note stacklight state and color(s)
actions.exact_action: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

steps.title: If horn alarm pattern is indicated, determine long vs intermittent horn during flashing
steps.purpose: Some documented stacklight patterns include horn alarm timing; capturing it improves status mapping accuracy.
steps.instruction: If the source indicates a horn alarm pattern for the flashing state you are seeing, also observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern.
steps.expected_result: You have determined whether the horn alarm is long or intermittent during the flashing pattern.
steps.healthy_condition: Horn alarm timing is clearly distinguishable as long vs intermittent while the stacklight is flashing.
steps.failure_condition: Horn alarm timing cannot be distinguished (e.g., noise/unclear audio).

actions.label: Determine horn alarm timing
actions.exact_action: Observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern.

steps.title: Match the observed stacklight pattern to the documented tipper/station status meanings
steps.purpose: Convert the observed solid/flashing color (and horn timing when applicable) into the documented status.
steps.instruction: Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings for tipper/station status, including RMS error, E-stop, tipping state, and surepost/bagout indications.
steps.expected_result: You can map the observed stacklight solid/flashing color combination (and horn timing when present) to one documented status.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed pattern matches one of the documented combinations (examples include Solid Blue, Solid Green, Solid Red, Solid White, Solid Red+Yellow+Green, Flashing Blue, Flashing Green, Flashing Red, Flashing White, Flashing Yellow, and horn-timed combinations).
steps.failure_condition: The observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination.

actions.label: Map stacklight pattern to documented status
actions.exact_action: Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings: Solid Blue (Tipper paused), Solid Green (Tipping in process), Solid Red (Estop activated), Solid White (AGV present post-tipping), Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error), Flashing Blue (Tipper disabled), Flashing Green (Tipper starved), Flashing Red (Tipper faulted), Flashing White (SurePost tote being sent), Flashing Yellow (AGV present pre-tipping), Flashing Green+Yellow+Green with long horn alarm (Sort starting), Flashing White with intermittent horn alarm (Bagout complete).

stop_or_escalate_if: Observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination

steps.title: Stop and escalate for E-stop activated or RMS error
steps.purpose: Ensure critical conditions are handled appropriately and not cleared via this interpretation procedure.
steps.instruction: If the mapped status indicates E-stop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green), stop and escalate immediately.
steps.expected_result: You have identified whether the mapped status is Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) and escalated accordingly.
steps.healthy_condition: Mapped status is not Solid Red (E-stop activated) and not Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error).
steps.failure_condition: Mapped status is Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) and escalation is not initiated.

actions.label: Escalate critical condition
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the observed stacklight pattern indicates Estop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green).

stop_or_escalate_if: Solid Red indicates Estop is activated
Solid Red+Yellow+Green indicates an RMS error

success_criteria: Operator can map the observed stacklight solid/flashing color combination (and horn timing when present) to a documented tipper/station status.
Operator escalates immediately when the mapped status indicates Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error).
healthy_conditions: Stacklight pattern matches a documented combination and indicates a non-critical state (i.e., not Solid Red or Solid Red+Yellow+Green).
failure_conditions: Observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination.
Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) is present and escalation is not initiated.
escalation_guidance: If Solid Red indicates Estop is activated: escalate immediately; do not attempt to clear remotely from this procedure.
If Solid Red+Yellow+Green indicates an RMS error: escalate for further diagnostics.
