content.text: Hands-on installation procedure for replacing an OptiSweep timing belt and setting counter-balance leg belt tension to the specified target (471 N) using equal tensioning of two screws and (optionally) a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, followed by torque/fastener steps and operator-station restart.

structured_payload.title: Install and tension a replacement timing belt (counter-balance leg) to 471 N
structured_payload.summary: Hands-on installation procedure for replacing an OptiSweep timing belt and setting counter-balance leg belt tension to the specified target (471 N) using equal tensioning of two screws and (optionally) a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, followed by torque/fastener steps and operator-station restart.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when replacing the OptiSweep timing belt and you must set the counter-balance leg belt tension to 471 N (acceptable range 448–494 N) before reassembly and restarting the operator station.
safety_notes: Perform the procedure with physical access to the timing belt assembly and use the specified PPE/tools (safety glasses, gloves) as applicable to the manual’s related maintenance context.
If using the sonic tension meter, note that excessive noise (e.g., forklifts beeping, conveyors running) can interfere with stable readings.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the timing belt assembly
Torque tool capable of 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs)
Fasteners/tools for M6x35, M8x25, and M6x20 screws

access_required: Physical access to the timing belt assembly
external_references: “Starting The Operator Station” referenced in the manual (page 66)

visual_references.description: Timing belt replacement figure showing timing belt assembly and pre-positioning of A-axis and counterbalance between threaded holes (context for belt access).
Idler pulley assembly figure (context for idler assembly and belt tensioning hardware).
Counterbalance weight figure (context for counterbalance carriage/hard stop behavior).
Gearbox figure (context for belt tensioning components and fastener locations).

steps.title: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys
steps.purpose: Install the replacement belt onto the pulley path before tensioning and securing.
steps.instruction: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys.
steps.expected_result: The replacement timing belt is seated on the pulleys in the intended routing path, ready for counter-balance positioning and tensioning.
steps.healthy_condition: Belt is correctly positioned on the pulleys with no obvious misrouting before tensioning.
steps.failure_condition: Belt is not seated on the pulleys or is visibly misrouted such that tensioning would be incorrect.

actions.label: Seat belt on pulleys
actions.exact_action: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys.

steps.title: Position counter-balance carriage on lower hard stop
steps.purpose: Set the counter-balance carriage to the correct resting position so the belt can be tensioned properly.
steps.instruction: Slightly lift the counter-balance carriage, remove the M6 fastener supporting it, and lower the counter-balance carriage to rest on the lower hard stop.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance carriage is resting on the lower hard stop after the M6 fastener is removed.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriage rests on the lower hard stop (not suspended) with the supporting M6 fastener removed.
steps.failure_condition: Carriage remains lifted/suspended or does not rest on the lower hard stop after removing the M6 fastener.

actions.label: Lift, remove M6, lower to hard stop
actions.exact_action: Slightly lift the counter-balance carriage, remove the M6 fastener supporting it, and lower the counter-balance carriage to rest on the lower hard stop.

steps.title: Very lightly tighten M8x25 idler assembly screws
steps.purpose: Hold the idler pulley assembly in place while still allowing it to slide under the fasteners during tensioning.
steps.instruction: Very lightly tighten the M8x25 screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place so the assembly is not loose, but it can slide under the fasteners.
steps.expected_result: Idler pulley assembly is held snugly (not loose) but can still slide under the M8x25 fasteners during tension adjustment.
steps.healthy_condition: Assembly does not rattle/shift freely, yet tensioning can move it as tension increases.
steps.failure_condition: Assembly is too loose (moves excessively) or too tight (does not allow sliding during tensioning).

actions.label: Lightly snug idler assembly
actions.exact_action: Very lightly tighten the M8x25 screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place so the assembly is not loose, but it can slide under the fasteners.

steps.title: Insert M6x35 tension screws to firm contact
steps.purpose: Establish initial contact points for tensioning the belt via the actuator base.
steps.instruction: Insert the two M6x35 tension screws until they make firm contact with the actuator base.
steps.expected_result: Both M6x35 tension screws are inserted and each makes firm contact with the actuator base.
steps.healthy_condition: No gap between each screw tip and the actuator base at the contact point.
steps.failure_condition: One or both screws are not contacting the actuator base (insufficient insertion).

actions.label: Seat tension screws
actions.exact_action: Insert the two M6x35 tension screws until they make firm contact with the actuator base.

steps.title: Equally tighten tension screws
steps.purpose: Apply belt tension evenly by turning both tension screws the same amount/force.
steps.instruction: Equally tighten the tension screws to add tension to the belt, ensuring both screws are turned the exact same amount (same applied force).
steps.expected_result: Both tension screws have been advanced equally, producing balanced belt tension increase.
steps.healthy_condition: No visible imbalance between the two tension screw positions/advancement; tension increases evenly.
steps.failure_condition: One screw is advanced more than the other (unequal applied force), leading to uneven tension.

actions.label: Equal turns on both screws
actions.exact_action: Equally tighten the tension screws… ensuring both screws are turned the exact same amount (same applied force).

steps.title: Increase tension to 471 N (448–494 N acceptable range)
steps.purpose: Bring belt tension to the specified target before locking the idler assembly.
steps.instruction: Gradually increase tension until 471 N is reached (acceptable range 448 N to 494 N).
steps.expected_result: Measured belt tension reaches 471 N within the acceptable range of 448–494 N.
steps.healthy_condition: Tension reading is within 448–494 N and as close to 471 N as practical.
steps.failure_condition: Tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range.

actions.label: Adjust until target tension
actions.exact_action: Gradually increase tension until 471 N is reached (acceptable range 448 N to 494 N).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range.

steps.title: Check tension only on the counter-balance leg
steps.purpose: Ensure the tension measurement corresponds to the correct belt segment.
steps.instruction: Check tension only on the counter-balance leg of the belt (counter-balance is not in the way and will not interfere with belt vibration).
steps.expected_result: Tension measurement is taken on the counter-balance leg only.
steps.healthy_condition: Measurement location is on the counter-balance leg and counter-balance does not interfere with belt vibration.
steps.failure_condition: Tension is checked on a different leg or counter-balance interferes with belt vibration during measurement.

actions.label: Measure correct belt leg
actions.exact_action: Check tension only on the counter-balance leg of the belt…

steps.title: Set Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter parameters (if used)
steps.purpose: Configure the sonic tension meter to the correct belt parameters for accurate readings.
steps.instruction: If using a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, set: Mass = 4.86 g/m, Width = 20 mm, Span = 1200 mm.
steps.expected_result: Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter is configured with Mass 4.86 g/m, Width 20 mm, Span 1200 mm.
steps.healthy_condition: Meter settings match the specified values before taking tension readings.
steps.failure_condition: Meter settings are not set to the specified values, leading to incorrect tension readings.

actions.label: Configure sonic meter
actions.exact_action: If using a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, set: Mass = 4.86 g/m, Width = 20 mm, Span = 1200 mm.

steps.title: Obtain three acceptable sonic readings in a row
steps.purpose: Verify stable tension measurement before locking the idler assembly.
steps.instruction: Adjust/check until three acceptable readings in a row are received. Note: excessive noise (e.g., forklifts beeping, conveyors running) can interfere with sonic meter readings.
steps.expected_result: Three consecutive sonic tension readings are acceptable.
steps.healthy_condition: Readings remain stable and acceptable across three consecutive checks.
steps.failure_condition: Three consecutive acceptable readings cannot be obtained, or readings are unstable due to excessive noise.

actions.label: Stabilize and re-check
actions.exact_action: Adjust/check until three acceptable readings in a row are received.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if three consecutive acceptable sonic meter readings cannot be obtained.
If excessive noise prevents stable sonic readings, reduce noise sources and re-check tension.

steps.title: Torque M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs)
steps.purpose: Lock the idler pulley assembly in place after achieving correct belt tension.
steps.instruction: Tighten the M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs) to lock the idler assembly in place.
steps.expected_result: M8x25 fasteners are torqued to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs), locking the idler assembly.
steps.healthy_condition: Fasteners are tightened to the specified torque value using the torque tool.
steps.failure_condition: Idler assembly is not locked (e.g., fasteners not torqued to spec) or tension shifts after tightening.

actions.label: Torque idler fasteners
actions.exact_action: Tighten the M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs) to lock the idler assembly in place.

steps.title: Raise counter-balance carriage and insert M6 socket-head screws
steps.purpose: Set the counter-balance carriage to mid-travel and secure it with the specified screws before clamp reattachment.
steps.instruction: Raise the counter-balance carriage back to mid-travel and insert the M6 socket-head screws for the carriage to rest against.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance carriage is at mid-travel and supported/resting against the inserted M6 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriage is positioned at mid-travel with screws installed as the rest support.
steps.failure_condition: Carriage is not at mid-travel or screws are not inserted to provide the rest support.

actions.label: Set mid-travel rest
actions.exact_action: Raise the counter-balance carriage back to mid-travel and insert the M6 socket-head screws for the carriage to rest against.

steps.title: Re-attach A-axis belt clamp with M6x20 screws and Loctite®
steps.purpose: Secure the A-axis belt clamp while ensuring the belt is not pinched and clamp aligns with belt teeth.
steps.instruction: Re-attach the A-axis belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring the belt clamp aligns with belt teeth and does not pinch the belt (belt may need slight movement to line up).
steps.expected_result: A-axis belt clamp is reattached with six M6x20 screws using Loctite®, aligned with belt teeth, and belt is not pinched.
steps.healthy_condition: Clamp teeth alignment matches belt teeth; belt can move/seat without being pinched by the clamp.
steps.failure_condition: Belt clamp is misaligned with belt teeth or pinches the belt.

actions.label: Attach A-axis belt clamp
actions.exact_action: Re-attach the A-axis belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring the belt clamp aligns with belt teeth and does not pinch the belt (belt may need slight movement to line up).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check clamp alignment if the belt appears pinched or the belt clamp does not align with belt teeth.

steps.title: Re-attach counter-balance belt clamp with M6x20 screws and Loctite®
steps.purpose: Secure the counter-balance belt clamp while ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch.
steps.instruction: Re-attach the counter-balance belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch (counter-balance may need to be lifted slightly for alignment).
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance belt clamp is reattached with six M6x20 screws using Loctite®, aligned with belt teeth, and belt is not pinched.
steps.healthy_condition: Clamp alignment matches belt teeth; belt is free of pinch points.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance belt clamp is misaligned or pinches the belt.

actions.label: Attach counter-balance belt clamp
actions.exact_action: Re-attach the counter-balance belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch (counter-balance may need to be lifted slightly for alignment).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check clamp alignment if the belt appears pinched or the belt clamp does not align with belt teeth.

steps.title: Remove M6 socket-head screws supporting A-axis and counter-balance
steps.purpose: Remove temporary supports once clamps are installed.
steps.instruction: Remove the M6 socket-head screws supporting the A-axis and counter-balance.
steps.expected_result: The M6 socket-head screws that supported the A-axis and counter-balance are removed.
steps.healthy_condition: No remaining support screws; A-axis and counter-balance are held by the installed belt/clamps as intended.
steps.failure_condition: Support screws remain installed when they should be removed, or removal destabilizes the assembly.

actions.label: Remove support screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the M6 socket-head screws supporting the A-axis and counter-balance.

steps.title: Reinstall side panels
steps.purpose: Restore station enclosure after belt/clamp installation.
steps.instruction: Reinstall the side panels.
steps.expected_result: Side panels are reinstalled.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panels are back in place, covering the belt/tensioning area.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels not fully reinstalled or left open after completion.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the side panels.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.purpose: Return the station to service after mechanical work is complete.
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.expected_result: Operator station is restarted per the manual’s referenced restart procedure.
steps.healthy_condition: Station restart completes successfully (no immediate mechanical issues attributable to belt/clamp pinch or incorrect tension).
steps.failure_condition: Restart fails or immediate issues indicate belt/clamp problems (e.g., belt pinch, tension not within target).

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).

success_criteria: Belt tension is set to 471 N within the acceptable range (448–494 N).
If using the Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter: three acceptable readings are obtained in a row.
Idler assembly is locked by tightening M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs).
Belt clamps (A-axis and counter-balance) are aligned with belt teeth and do not pinch the belt.
healthy_conditions: Tension reading is within 448–494 N and as close to 471 N as possible.
Three consecutive sonic meter readings are acceptable (when sonic meter is used).
M8x25 fasteners are torqued to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs).
Belt clamps align with belt teeth and belt is not pinched.
failure_conditions: Tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range.
Three consecutive acceptable sonic meter readings cannot be obtained.
Belt clamp alignment is incorrect or belt appears pinched.
Excessive noise prevents stable sonic readings.
escalation_guidance: If tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range or acceptable sonic readings cannot be obtained, stop and re-check the tensioning process (including equal screw advancement and measurement location on the counter-balance leg).
If belt clamp alignment is incorrect or the belt is pinched, stop and re-check clamp alignment before restarting the operator station.

content.text: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper station for timing belt replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counterbalance between the actuator-base threaded holes, performing site “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on the tipper, removing the nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners to access the timing belt, and threading M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.

structured_payload.title: Remove Timing Belt on Tipper Station (A-axis/counterbalance positioning, LOTO, side panel removal, belt access)
structured_payload.summary: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper station for timing belt replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counterbalance between the actuator-base threaded holes, performing site “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on the tipper, removing the nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners to access the timing belt, and threading M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this procedure when preparing the tipper station for timing belt replacement and you must (1) position the A-axis/counterbalance correctly, (2) lock out/tag out the tipper using the site Operator Station LOTO process, (3) remove the station side panels to access the timing belt, and (4) install M6 socket-head screws below both carriages before releasing belt tension.
not_for: Do not proceed to belt tension release unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform on-site physical positioning, execute site Operator Station Lockout/Tagout for the tipper, remove side panels, and install the M6 socket-head screws as specified.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the site’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” process before removing side panels or accessing belt components.
Do not release belt tension unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent the A-axis/counterbalance from dropping.

access_required: Physical access to the tipper station
system_preconditions: Tipper station is ready for maintenance access (side panels can be removed after LOTO).

steps.title: Manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between actuator-base threaded holes
steps.purpose: Place the A-axis/counterbalance in the correct safe position so the station side panels can be removed and the belt access/prevent-drop screws can be installed.
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: The A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes on their respective rails (two holes adjacent to each rail).
steps.healthy_condition: Both carriages are visibly located between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail (not outside the hole pair).
steps.failure_condition: One or both carriages are not between the threaded holes on their respective rails.

actions.label: Position A-axis/counterbalance
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check positioning if the carriages are not between the threaded holes on their respective rails.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the site Operator Station Lockout/Tagout process
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely de-energized/locked out before removing side panels and accessing the timing belt area.
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the site’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” process.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a locked-out/tagged-out state per the site Operator Station Lockout/Tagout process.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed and verified for the tipper before proceeding to side panel removal.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed/verified for the tipper.

actions.label: Execute site LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed/verified for the tipper.

steps.title: Remove the nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners and remove side panels to access the timing belt
steps.purpose: Expose the timing belt so the belt replacement preparation can continue.
steps.instruction: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panels, then remove the station side panels to access the timing belt.
steps.expected_result: The nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners are removed and the station side panels are off, exposing the timing belt access area.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panels are removed and the timing belt area is accessible without obstruction.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels remain secured (fasteners not fully removed) or timing belt access is obstructed.

actions.label: Remove side-panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panels then remove the station side panels to access the timing belt.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws into holes below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Mechanically prevent the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping when belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are installed in the holes below both carriages.
steps.healthy_condition: Both sets of holes below the carriages have M6 socket-head screws threaded in place (prevent-drop condition established).
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws are not installed below one or both carriages.

actions.label: Install M6 prevent-drop screws
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not release belt tension unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping.

success_criteria: A-axis and counterbalance are positioned between the actuator-base threaded holes with carriages between the holes on their respective rails.
Tipper is LOTO’d using the site Operator Station Lockout/Tagout process.
Nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners are removed and side panels are off to access the timing belt.
M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
healthy_conditions: Carriages are between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
LOTO is completed/verified for the tipper before side panel removal.
Side panels are removed and timing belt access area is exposed.
M6 socket-head screws are installed below both carriages.
failure_conditions: Carriages are not between the threaded holes on their respective rails.
LOTO cannot be completed/verified for the tipper.
Side panels cannot be removed because the nine self-tapping fasteners are not fully removed.
M6 socket-head screws are missing below one or both carriages, making belt tension release unsafe.
escalation_guidance: If positioning is incorrect, stop and re-check carriage placement between the threaded holes on their respective rails before continuing.
If LOTO cannot be completed/verified for the tipper, stop and do not proceed.
If M6 socket-head screws cannot be installed below both carriages, stop and do not release belt tension.

actions.label: Apply tape/marker marks

actions.label: Cut cable ties

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if the cable is still attached by an uncut cable tie near the A-axis PCA (the procedure notes there may be one more cable tie to cut near the PCA).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.15.1 REMOVAL step 9: "Unplug the cable from the A-axis PCA and remove it from the cable carrier. There may be one more cable tie to cut near the PCA."

content.text: Safely remove a failed OptiSweep tipper from its station by applying lockout/tagout (LOTO) and disconnecting the tipper’s power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet (ClearLink controller), air line (quick disconnect), and the conduit bringing power/air/Ethernet to the column. Optionally remove the gripper and counter-balance weights before unbolting the tipper.

structured_payload.title: Remove a Tipper (LOTO + disconnect power/air/Ethernet/conduit) for Tipper Replacement
structured_payload.summary: Safely remove a failed OptiSweep tipper from its station by applying lockout/tagout (LOTO) and disconnecting the tipper’s power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet (ClearLink controller), air line (quick disconnect), and the conduit bringing power/air/Ethernet to the column. Optionally remove the gripper and counter-balance weights before unbolting the tipper.

Do not use if you cannot complete LOTO or cannot safely disconnect any of the required connections as described.

safety_notes: Apply LOTO to the tipper before disconnecting power/Ethernet/air/conduit.
Keep the tipper supported while removing the mounting screws.

content.text: Preventive maintenance for an OptiSweep tipper: visually inspect the Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease. If the rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks through the grease nipples using automotive bearing grease, applying 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block. Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication.

structured_payload.title: Inspect and Lubricate Tipper Z-Axis Linear Bearings (Grease Wetness on Z-Axis Linear Rails)
structured_payload.summary: Preventive maintenance for an OptiSweep tipper: visually inspect the Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease. If the rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks through the grease nipples using automotive bearing grease, applying 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block. Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use during tipper preventive maintenance to check Z-axis linear rail lubrication condition (wet grease vs dried grease) and to apply grease to the Z-axis bearing blocks when the rails are dry.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the visual inspection of both Z-axis linear rails and, if dry, lubricate the bearing blocks via the grease nipples with automotive bearing grease using the specified quantity per block.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to both Z-axis linear rails and the bearing blocks
Grease applicator capable of delivering 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block

access_required: Physical access to both Z-axis linear rails and the bearing blocks

visual_references.description: End stop assembly diagram (included in packet artifacts; not specifically tied to grease nipple location for this procedure).

steps.title: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease
steps.purpose: Determine whether lubrication is present (wet grease) or absent (dry/dried grease) to decide whether lubrication is required.
steps.instruction: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails and look for wet grease and/or signs of dried grease.
steps.expected_result: You can classify the condition of the Z-axis linear rails as either wet with grease or dry (not wet with grease) / showing dried grease.
steps.healthy_condition: Rails show grease wetness and/or signs of dried grease (indicating grease presence).
steps.failure_condition: Rails are dry (not wet with grease), indicating lubrication is needed.

actions.label: Inspect Z-axis rails
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease. If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

steps.title: If rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease
steps.purpose: Restore lubrication to the Z-axis bearing blocks when the rails are dry.
steps.instruction: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease), lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).
steps.expected_result: Grease is applied to the bearing blocks via the grease nipples using the specified quantity per block (1.0 to 3.0 cc per block).
steps.healthy_condition: Grease is applied to each bearing block through its grease nipples with 1.0 to 3.0 cc per block.
steps.failure_condition: Grease is not applied to the bearing blocks (or lubrication is attempted by wiping rails instead of greasing the bearing blocks).

actions.label: Lubricate bearing blocks
actions.exact_action: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

stop_or_escalate_if: If rails show signs of dried grease but lubrication cannot be performed as specified (e.g., inability to access nipples), stop and escalate to maintenance support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

steps.title: Locate the grease nipples on the two bearing blocks
steps.purpose: Ensure grease is applied to the correct lubrication points (the bearing blocks via the nipples).
steps.instruction: Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).
steps.expected_result: You identify four (4) grease nipples total: two bearing blocks, one 1/4-in nipple on each end of each block.
steps.healthy_condition: All four nipples are located and accessible for greasing the bearing blocks.
steps.failure_condition: Nipples cannot be located or accessed, preventing lubrication as specified.

actions.label: Find grease nipples
actions.exact_action: Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the nipples to apply grease to the bearing blocks, stop and escalate to maintenance support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: There are two (2) bearing blocks with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end each, so there are four (4) nipples to grease.

steps.title: Apply 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block
steps.purpose: Apply the specified grease quantity to ensure adequate lubrication of each bearing block.
steps.instruction: Using a grease applicator, add 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block (via its grease nipples).
steps.expected_result: Total grease applied per bearing block is within 1.0 to 3.0 cc, and grease has been delivered through the bearing block nipples.
steps.healthy_condition: Each bearing block receives 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease (four nipples total used to deliver grease to the two blocks).
steps.failure_condition: Grease quantity per block is outside 1.0 to 3.0 cc, or grease is not delivered to the bearing blocks through the nipples.

actions.label: Grease bearing blocks
actions.exact_action: Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate.

steps.title: Do not substitute wiping grease on the rails for lubrication
steps.purpose: Ensure lubrication is performed correctly at the bearing blocks rather than only cosmetically on the rails.
steps.instruction: Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease. If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™). There are two (2) bearing blocks with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end each, so there are four (4) nipples to grease. Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate. NOTE: Wiping grease on the rails is not adequate.

content.text: Prepare the OptiSweep Z-axis for gearbox replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counter-balance to the specified threaded-hole location using the tipper HMI, performing tipper lockout/tagout (LOTO), removing the station side panel (nine self-tapping fasteners), and exposing the motor/gearbox area. Install an M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.

structured_payload.title: Remove Z-Axis Gearbox for OptiSweep Z-Axis Gearbox Replacement (A-axis jog + LOTO + side panel removal)
structured_payload.summary: Prepare the OptiSweep Z-axis for gearbox replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counter-balance to the specified threaded-hole location using the tipper HMI, performing tipper lockout/tagout (LOTO), removing the station side panel (nine self-tapping fasteners), and exposing the motor/gearbox area. Install an M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when preparing an OptiSweep Z-axis gearbox replacement and you must (1) position the A-axis/counter-balance between the actuator-base threaded holes, (2) lockout/tagout the tipper, and (3) remove the station side panel to access the motor/gearbox area.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a complete gearbox replacement workflow (it only covers the removal preparation steps evidenced in the provided manual section/page excerpt).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the A-axis/counter-balance jog on the tipper HMI, execute tipper LOTO using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure, remove the nine side-panel fasteners, remove the station side panel, and install the M6 socket-head screw below both carriages.
safety_notes: Perform tipper LOTO using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
Stop if the A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned as described or cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to tipper station for LOTO and side panel removal

access_required: tipper_hmi (WebVisu/VISU operator station HMI)
Physical access to the tipper station
system_preconditions: Tipper is capable of manual jog positioning of the A-axis and counter-balance via the tipper HMI.
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure on page 2 (referenced by the manual for tipper LOTO).

visual_references.description: Figure 7-7: Gearbox diagram supporting the removal preparation steps (A-axis/counter-balance positioning, tipper LOTO reference, nine side-panel fasteners, and M6 socket-head screw below both carriages).

steps.title: Jog A-axis and counter-balance to the threaded-hole position
steps.purpose: Position the A-axis/counter-balance so the gearbox removal preparation can proceed safely and so the carriages can be secured to prevent dropping after belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: On the tipper HMI (WebVisu/VISU), manually position (jog) the A-axis and counter-balance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: A-axis/counter-balance are positioned between the threaded holes with carriages between the holes on their respective rails.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are visibly located between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail (as shown in the gearbox figure).
steps.failure_condition: A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, or carriages cannot be placed between the holes on their respective rails.

actions.label: Manual jog A-axis/counter-balance
actions.exact_action: Use the HMI to manually position (jog) the A-axis and counter-balance between the threaded holes in the actuator base.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.

steps.title: Perform tipper LOTO using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before removing the station side panel and accessing the motor/gearbox area.
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO for the tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
steps.expected_result: Tipper is locked out/tagged out.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed for the tipper per the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (page 2).
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.

actions.label: Execute tipper lockout/tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.

steps.title: Remove the station side panel fasteners and the station side panel
steps.purpose: Expose the motor/gearbox access area by removing the station side panel secured with nine self-tapping fasteners.
steps.instruction: Using a 3/8-in. wrench or socket, remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed and the motor/gearbox access area is exposed.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine self-tapping fasteners are removed and the station side panel is removed without remaining fasteners attached.
steps.failure_condition: Fasteners cannot be removed with the 3/8-in. wrench/socket, or the side panel cannot be removed to access the motor.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Install M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Prevent the A-axis and counter-balance from dropping once belt tension is released during subsequent gearbox removal steps.
steps.instruction: Insert an M6 socket-head screw into the holes below both carriages. These fasteners prevent the A-axis and counter-balance from dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: An M6 socket-head screw is installed into the holes below both carriages.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screw(s) are seated in the holes below both carriages, providing mechanical retention as described.
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screw cannot be inserted into the holes below both carriages, or the carriages cannot be held in place.

actions.label: Insert M6 screw below carriages
actions.exact_action: Insert an M6 socket-head screw into the holes below both carriages.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the carriages cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.

success_criteria: A-axis/counter-balance are positioned between the threaded holes with carriages between the holes on their respective rails.
Tipper is locked out/tagged out using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (page 2).
Station side panel is removed and the motor/gearbox access area is exposed.
M6 socket-head screw is installed below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
healthy_conditions: Carriages are between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
LOTO is completed for the tipper per the referenced procedure (page 2).

M6 socket-head screw is installed below both carriages.
failure_conditions: A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.

Side panel cannot be removed to access the motor.
Carriages cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.
escalation_guidance: If any stop condition is met (positioning, LOTO, side panel removal, or M6 screw retention), stop work and escalate per site maintenance escalation process (not specified in the provided packet).

content.text: Performs a quick Z-axis cable carrier replacement by LOTO the tipper, snapping the carrier apart at both ends, removing the old carrier, installing the new carrier, snapping cross bars closed, and snapping both ends into the end pieces that remain mounted.

structured_payload.title: Quick Replacement of Z-Axis Cable Carrier (Snap Apart/Ends Snap-In)
structured_payload.summary: Performs a quick Z-axis cable carrier replacement by LOTO the tipper, snapping the carrier apart at both ends, removing the old carrier, installing the new carrier, snapping cross bars closed, and snapping both ends into the end pieces that remain mounted.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when both ends of the existing Z-axis cable carrier are in good condition and you need a quick replacement by snapping the carrier apart at both ends, leaving the end pieces mounted on the tipper.
not_for: Do not use this quick replacement method if either end of the existing carrier is not in good condition (the procedure is explicitly a quick replacement only when both ends are good).
Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed safely or if access to the motor/side panel is unclear.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform LOTO on the tipper and execute the physical cable carrier replacement steps (side panel removal if necessary, snap-apart/snap-in actions, and reassembly).
safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper before removing the side panel or disassembling the cable carrier.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the tipper and station side panel

access_required: physical_floor
system_preconditions: Both ends of the existing Z-axis cable carrier are in good condition (required for quick replacement).
Tipper can be safely LOTO.

content.text: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, update the replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner’s Barcode Interface settings so tote/location label prefixes match and the HTTP/OPC URLs point to the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses, then save the settings.

structured_payload.title: Configure Barcode Interface scanner settings (password, prefixes, HTTP/OPC URLs) for AGV and Hospital control IPs
structured_payload.summary: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, update the replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner’s Barcode Interface settings so tote/location label prefixes match and the HTTP/OPC URLs point to the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses, then save the settings.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when a scanner is replaced and the new scanner must be set up so Barcode Interface settings use the correct tote/location prefixes and the correct AGV/Hospital control IP addresses in the HTTP and OPC URL fields.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the Barcode Interface settings update (enter password, verify prefixes, update HTTP/OPC URLs, save settings).

access_required: FORTNA account login on the Windows laptop
system_preconditions: Network connectivity from the laptop to both the AGV control and Hospital control (validated by ping per scanner setup requirements).
Barcode Interface application is installed on the Windows laptop (found on the desktop with a FORTNA logo).

visual_references.description: Scanner Setup screen showing the settings button/password prompt, prefix fields, HTTP URL field (AGV control IP), OPC URL field (Hospital control IP), and Save Settings button.

steps.title: Launch Barcode Interface on the scanner setup laptop
steps.purpose: Open the application used to configure the replacement scanner settings.
steps.instruction: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, launch the Barcode Interface application (Barcode Interface.exe).
steps.expected_result: Barcode Interface is open and ready for interaction (scanner setup workflow visible).
steps.healthy_condition: The application is running and you can proceed to the settings area.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface does not launch or is not accessible on the desktop.

actions.label: Open Barcode Interface
actions.exact_action: Launch the Barcode Interface application. This should be on the desktop.

steps.title: Open Settings and enter the default password
steps.purpose: Access the protected settings panel to edit prefixes and HTTP/OPC URLs.
steps.instruction: In Barcode Interface, click the "settings" button and supply the default password "Opti".
steps.expected_result: The settings panel accepts the password and the settings fields are available for editing.
steps.healthy_condition: You can view/edit the prefix configuration fields and the HTTP/OPC URL fields.
steps.failure_condition: Password is rejected or settings fields do not become available.

actions.label: Open settings
actions.exact_action: Check the settings by clicking the settings button, supply the password. By default, the pass- word is “Opti”.

steps.title: Verify tote/location label prefixes match
steps.purpose: Ensure the scanner will interpret labels correctly for totes and locations.
steps.instruction: Verify the configured prefixes match the labels on the totes and locations.
steps.expected_result: Prefix values shown in the settings match the tote/location label prefixes you physically verify.
steps.healthy_condition: Prefixes match the tote/location labels (no mismatch observed).
steps.failure_condition: Prefixes do not match the tote/location labels.

actions.label: Compare prefixes
actions.exact_action: Verify prefixes match the labels on the totes and locations.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the prefixes do not match the tote/location labels.

steps.title: Update HTTP and OPC URLs to correct AGV/Hospital control IPs
steps.purpose: Point the scanner interface to the correct AGV control and Hospital control endpoints.
steps.instruction: Change the URL for both the HTTP and OPC settings so the HTTP URL contains the AGV control IP address and the OPC URL contains the Hospital control IP address.
steps.expected_result: HTTP URL field includes the AGV control IP address; OPC URL field includes the Hospital control IP address.
steps.healthy_condition: Both URL fields contain the correct IP addresses in the expected HTTP vs OPC fields.
steps.failure_condition: HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.

actions.label: Edit HTTP/OPC URLs
actions.exact_action: Change the URL for both the HTTP and OPC setting to contain the AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses respectively.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.

steps.title: Save the scanner settings
steps.purpose: Commit the updated prefixes and URLs so the scanner uses them.
steps.instruction: Save the settings using the "Save Settings" button.
steps.expected_result: Settings are saved (the updated prefix/URL values are committed after clicking "Save Settings").
steps.healthy_condition: After saving, the settings reflect the updated prefixes and the HTTP/OPC URLs with the correct IP addresses.
steps.failure_condition: Settings do not save or the displayed values revert/are not updated after saving.

actions.label: Save settings
actions.exact_action: Save the settings with the "Save Settings" button.

success_criteria: After saving, the Barcode Interface settings reflect prefixes matching tote/location labels.
After saving, the HTTP URL contains the AGV control IP address and the OPC URL contains the Hospital control IP address.
healthy_conditions: Prefix fields match tote/location labels.
HTTP URL field contains AGV control IP address.
OPC URL field contains Hospital control IP address.
Settings are saved via the "Save Settings" button.
failure_conditions: Prefixes do not match tote/location labels.
HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.
Settings do not persist after clicking "Save Settings".
escalation_guidance: If prefixes do not match tote/location labels, stop and escalate.
If HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses, stop and escalate.

content.text: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner so the Barcode Interface application shows healthy connectivity and the scanner is calibrated when the app connectivity indicator is red.

structured_payload.title: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner using Barcode Interface (hardware connect + connectivity + calibration)
structured_payload.summary: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner so the Barcode Interface application shows healthy connectivity and the scanner is calibrated when the app connectivity indicator is red.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when a Zebra DS3608-SR scanner has been replaced and needs setup so Barcode Interface connectivity is healthy; if the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator is red, calibration is required.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the scanner dock/cabling connection, launch Barcode Interface, verify the connectivity indicator, and run calibration when the indicator is red.
access_or_tools_needed: USB cable with RJ45 side (to dock) and USB to laptop
Network connectivity to the AGV control and Hospital control at the laptop (validated by pinging their IP addresses)

access_required: FORTNA account login on the Windows laptop
system_preconditions: Barcode Interface.exe is installed on the Windows 10/11 laptop (found on the desktop with a FORTNA logo).
Scanner dock, USB cable, and power adapter are available for the replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner.
Laptop has network connectivity to the AGV control and Hospital control (validated by pinging their IP addresses).

visual_references.description: Scanner Setup procedure image (hardware connections + dock power light + battery indicator note + connectivity/calibration decision).
Scanner Setup screen showing settings access (settings button), default password 'Opti', prefix verification, and HTTP/OPC URL fields with Save Settings.

steps.title: Verify laptop and Barcode Interface availability; log in with a FORTNA account
steps.purpose: Ensure the setup laptop can run Barcode Interface and is authenticated before connecting and configuring the scanner.
steps.instruction: On the Windows 10/11 laptop, confirm Barcode Interface.exe is installed (on the desktop with a FORTNA logo), then log into the laptop with a FORTNA account.
steps.expected_result: You are logged into the Windows laptop with a FORTNA account and Barcode Interface.exe is available to launch.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode Interface.exe is present on the desktop and you can proceed to launch it.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface.exe is not available or you cannot log in with a FORTNA account.

actions.label: Confirm Barcode Interface.exe and login
actions.exact_action: Log into the laptop with a FORTNA account.

steps.title: Connect scanner dock cabling and power; confirm dock lights up
steps.purpose: Provide power and connectivity path from the scanner dock to the laptop so the scanner can charge and Barcode Interface can detect connectivity.
steps.instruction: Connect the RJ45 side of the USB cable to the back of the scanner dock, connect the USB to the laptop, and connect the auxiliary cable to the power adapter. Plug the power adapter into a 120 VAC outlet (x2). Confirm the dock lights up.
steps.expected_result: The scanner dock powers on and its lights are on.
steps.healthy_condition: Dock lights up after the power adapter is plugged into a 120 VAC outlet.
steps.failure_condition: Dock does not light up after connecting power.

actions.label: Connect RJ45/USB/aux power
actions.exact_action: Connect the RJ45 side of the USB cable to the back of the scanner dock, the USB to the laptop, and the auxiliary to the power adapter. Be sure to plug the adapter into a 120 VAC outlet. The dock should light up.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the dock does not light up after connecting power.

steps.title: Charge the scanner on the dock until the battery indicator turns green
steps.purpose: Ensure the replacement scanner has sufficient charge before proceeding to Barcode Interface connectivity checks and calibration.
steps.instruction: If the scanner is uncharged, place it on the dock until the red battery symbol shown on top turns green.
steps.expected_result: Scanner battery indicator changes from red to green.
steps.healthy_condition: Battery indicator on top of the scanner is green.
steps.failure_condition: Battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.

actions.label: Check battery indicator color
actions.exact_action: If the scanner is uncharged it will need to rest on the dock until the red battery symbol shown on top turns green.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.

steps.title: Launch Barcode Interface application
steps.purpose: Open the application that displays connectivity status and provides the calibration action when connectivity is red.
steps.instruction: Launch the Barcode Interface application (should be on the desktop).
steps.expected_result: Barcode Interface is open and the screen is ready for connectivity status verification.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode Interface window is visible and you can view the connectivity indicator at the bottom right of the screen.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface does not launch or the connectivity indicator is not visible.

actions.label: Open Barcode Interface
actions.exact_action: Launch the Barcode Interface application. This should be on the desktop.

steps.title: Check Barcode Interface connectivity indicator (bottom right)
steps.purpose: Determine whether the scanner needs calibration based on the app connectivity status.
steps.instruction: Check the connectivity indicator at the bottom right of the Barcode Interface screen.
steps.expected_result: Connectivity indicator is either green or red.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator is green.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator remains red.

actions.label: Observe connectivity indicator
actions.exact_action: Check connectivity on the bottom right of the screen.

steps.title: Calibrate scanner only if connectivity indicator is red
steps.purpose: Restore healthy scanner connectivity by running calibration when the app reports red connectivity.
steps.instruction: If the connectivity indicator is red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions until calibration completes.
steps.expected_result: After calibration, the operator observes the connectivity indicator change to green.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator becomes green after calibration.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following the onscreen instructions.

actions.label: Run calibration
actions.exact_action: If red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following the onscreen instructions.

steps.title: Skip calibration if connectivity indicator is green
steps.purpose: Avoid unnecessary calibration when the scanner already reports healthy connectivity.
steps.instruction: If the connectivity indicator is green, skip calibration and proceed to the next step of the overall scanner setup procedure.
steps.expected_result: Connectivity indicator is green and calibration is not performed.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator is green.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator is not green (red) but calibration is skipped.

actions.label: Confirm green status
actions.exact_action: If green, skip this step.

success_criteria: Barcode Interface connectivity indicator at the bottom right is green.
If connectivity was red initially, calibration was run and the operator observes the connectivity indicator change to green.
Scanner battery indicator is green (if it was initially red).
healthy_conditions: Scanner dock lights up after power is connected.
Scanner battery indicator turns green after charging on the dock.
Barcode Interface connectivity indicator at bottom right is green.
failure_conditions: Dock does not light up after connecting power.
Scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.
Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following onscreen instructions.
escalation_guidance: If the dock does not light up after connecting power, stop and escalate.
If the scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock, stop and escalate.
If the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after calibration, stop and escalate.

content.text: Use the SMALLS overview screen on the System HMI to quickly identify which parts of the SMALLS system are in a normal vs abnormal (color-coded) status based on the system layout.

structured_payload.title: Check SMALLS System Health Using the Smalls Overview HMI Screen (Color-Coded Layout)
structured_payload.summary: Use the SMALLS overview screen on the System HMI to quickly identify which parts of the SMALLS system are in a normal vs abnormal (color-coded) status based on the system layout.
structured_payload.when_to_use: When you need a fast, at-a-glance health check of the SMALLS system parts using the color-coded SMALLS system layout.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Open the System HMI SMALLS overview screen and identify any parts showing abnormal color-coded status; stop/escalate when abnormal indications are widespread or unclear.
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU (System HMI access where the SMALLS button is available)

access_required: System HMI access where the SMALLS button is available (Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU)

visual_references.description: Figure 4-4: Smalls System Overview Screen (color-coded SMALLS system layout).

steps.title: Open the "Smalls" overview screen from the System HMI
steps.purpose: Get to the SMALLS overview layout that shows color-coded status for each part.
steps.instruction: On the System HMI, press the SMALLS button to open the "Smalls" overview screen.
steps.expected_result: The "Smalls" overview screen is displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen loads successfully and shows the SMALLS system layout.
steps.failure_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen does not open or the SMALLS layout is not visible.

actions.label: Press SMALLS
actions.exact_action: Press SMALLS to access the "Smalls" overview screen.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the "Smalls" overview screen, stop and escalate for support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Press SMALLS to access the "Smalls" overview screen. The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Review the SMALLS system layout on the "Smalls" overview screen
steps.purpose: Identify each SMALLS part shown on the layout so you can check its color-coded status.
steps.instruction: On the "Smalls" overview screen, review the SMALLS system layout.
steps.expected_result: You can see the SMALLS system layout with parts displayed for status checking.
steps.healthy_condition: The layout is fully visible and each part is present on the screen for color inspection.
steps.failure_condition: Parts are missing/unreadable on the layout, or the screen does not provide a clear view of the layout.

actions.label: Review layout
actions.exact_action: Review the "Smalls" system layout.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot clearly determine which parts are shown on the layout, stop and escalate.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Check each SMALLS part’s color-coded status indicator
steps.purpose: Determine which parts are abnormal by observing the color-coded status indicators on the layout.
steps.instruction: For each part shown on the layout, observe the color-coded status indicator.
steps.expected_result: You have identified which parts (if any) show abnormal color-coded status (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part).
steps.healthy_condition: All parts show the normal/expected color-coded status indicators for their respective parts.
steps.failure_condition: One or more parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.

actions.label: Observe color-coded indicators
actions.exact_action: Observe the color-coded status of each part of the system.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Identify abnormal parts and decide whether to stop/escalate
steps.purpose: Ensure abnormal indications are handled appropriately and escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.instruction: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part). If the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, treat it as abnormal.
steps.expected_result: You have a clear list of abnormal parts (if any) and a decision to escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: No parts indicate abnormal color-coded status; no offline/blocked section is indicated.
steps.failure_condition: Multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status, or the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, or you cannot determine which parts are abnormal.

actions.label: Identify abnormal parts
actions.exact_action: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.
Stop and escalate if the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.
Stop and escalate if you cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

success_criteria: Operator can open the "Smalls" overview screen and visually identify abnormal color-coded status indicators for any SMALLS parts.
Operator escalates when multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status or when abnormality is unclear.
healthy_conditions: All parts on the "Smalls" overview screen show normal/expected color-coded status indicators.
No offline/blocked section is indicated on the SMALLS layout.
failure_conditions: One or more SMALLS parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.
Multiple SMALLS parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.
The operator cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.
The layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.
escalation_guidance: If multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status, or if the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, stop and escalate for support.

content.text: Use the read-only Operator Station HMI screen VISU_IO_DIAG to troubleshoot operator-station I/O by verifying the displayed Control Temps (CPU and MB), internal controller Voltage Levels (expected 24 V), and the on/off status of the station switch and inputs. Use the input sections to open input detail information and use the screen drop-down to navigate to other screens if needed.

structured_payload.title: Check Operator Station HMI I/O Diagnostics (VISU_IO_DIAG) for CPU/MB Temps, 24V, and Input/ Switch States
structured_payload.summary: Use the read-only Operator Station HMI screen VISU_IO_DIAG to troubleshoot operator-station I/O by verifying the displayed Control Temps (CPU and MB), internal controller Voltage Levels (expected 24 V), and the on/off status of the station switch and inputs. Use the input sections to open input detail information and use the screen drop-down to navigate to other screens if needed.
structured_payload.when_to_use: When troubleshooting operator-station I/O on the Operator Station HMI and you need to confirm that the HMI hardware diagnostics are reporting expected values for CPU/MB temperatures, internal controller voltage (should be 24 V), and the station switch/input on/off indications.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Navigate the Operator Station HMI to the read-only VISU_IO_DIAG screen and verify the diagnostic sections (Control Temps, Voltage Levels, switch/input on/off).
safety_notes: VISU_IO_DIAG is a read-only screen used for troubleshooting.
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU access to the VISU_IO_DIAG screen

access_required: Operator Station HMI access to the VISU_IO_DIAG screen
system_preconditions: Operator Station HMI is powered on and the VISU_IO_DIAG screen is available

visual_references.description: Figure 4-27: Operator Station IO Diagnostics Screen (VISU_IO_DIAG) showing the informational banner, Control Temps (CPU/MB), Voltage Levels (expected 24 V), switch status (inputs on/off), input sections that open detail windows, and the drop-down menu.

steps.title: Open the read-only VISU_IO_DIAG diagnostics screen on the Operator Station HMI
steps.purpose: Access the diagnostic sections needed to verify CPU/MB temperatures, internal controller voltage (expected 24 V), and switch/input on/off states.
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI, navigate to the read-only screen named VISU_IO_DIAG (Operator Station IO Diagnostics Screen).
steps.expected_result: The VISU_IO_DIAG screen is open and displays the informational banner, the “Control Temps” section, the “Voltage Levels” section, the switch status section (inputs on/off), the input sections, and the drop-down menu.
steps.healthy_condition: VISU_IO_DIAG loads successfully and shows all diagnostic sections (banner, Control Temps, Voltage Levels, switch status, inputs, and drop-down menu).
steps.failure_condition: The VISU_IO_DIAG screen cannot be opened, or it does not display the Control Temps / Voltage Levels / input sections as described.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_IO_DIAG
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the read-only screen named VISU_IO_DIAG (Operator Station IO Diagnostics Screen).

stop_or_escalate_if: VISU_IO_DIAG cannot be opened or does not display the Control Temps / Voltage Levels / input sections.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: NOTE: This screen is read-only and can be used for troubleshooting. steps.title: Turn off power to the tipper using the disconnect

steps.failure_condition: Power remains on (HMI does not behave as expected for a power-on sequence).

steps.title: Hold the top three buttons on the tipper HMI

steps.expected_result: The top three buttons are held continuously in preparation for powering on.
steps.healthy_condition: Buttons remain held through the power-on in the next step.
steps.failure_condition: You release the buttons before or during power-on.

actions.label: Hold top three buttons
actions.exact_action: On the tipper HMI, press and hold the top three buttons.

steps.title: Power on the tipper while continuing to hold the top three buttons

actions.label: Power on tipper

steps.title: Wait for the gray screen

steps.healthy_condition: Gray screen is visible while buttons are still held.
steps.failure_condition: No gray screen appears.

actions.label: Confirm gray screen
actions.exact_action: Keep holding the buttons until a gray screen appears.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the gray screen does not appear, stop and re-check that the correct buttons are held through power-on before proceeding.

steps.failure_condition: USB is not inserted correctly (install option cannot proceed).

actions.exact_action: Plug the USB drive containing the new firmware version into the USB dongle on the HMI.

steps.expected_result: The HMI begins the firmware install flow from the USB.

steps.failure_condition: The install flow does not start or does not progress.

actions.label: Start install from USB
actions.exact_action: Press the "INSTALL FROM FILE" button.

steps.title: Load the firmware from the USB until the install completes

steps.healthy_condition: Install/load progress completes successfully and the flow ends.
steps.failure_condition: Install does not complete or appears stuck/failed.

actions.label: Run install flow to completion
actions.exact_action: Load the firmware from the USB (continue the on-screen install flow until it completes).

steps.title: Power-cycle the controller and boot normally

actions.exact_action: Press F3 to go to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.

steps.title: Verify green Process Status indicators in the Process Status section
steps.purpose: Confirm the tipper’s current operational state before using send/pause controls.
steps.instruction: In the Process Status section, observe the green status indicators for: In Cycle (Auto mode), Tipper Ready, AGV Present, Tip in Process, Tipper Clear, and Tipper Faulted.
steps.expected_result: The Process Status indicators show green states corresponding to the current tipper process state (as defined by the VISU_DATA Process Status indicators).
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant indicators you intend to rely on for the action are green (e.g., In Cycle is green when operating in Auto mode; Tipper Ready is green when ready to receive a tote; Tip in Process is green when the gripper has a tote; Tipper Clear is green when the gripper is open; Tipper Faulted is green if the tipper currently has a fault).
steps.failure_condition: The Process Status indicators do not match the intended action state (e.g., the tipper is not in the expected ready/clear/in-process state, or the tipper faulted state is not consistent with what you are attempting).

actions.exact_action: Observe the Process Status indicators (In Cycle, Tipper Ready, AGV Present, Tip in Process, Tipper Clear, Tipper Faulted).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Process Status indicators and meanings: In Cycle (green if operating in Auto mode), Tipper Ready (green if ready to receive a tote), AGV Present (green if a robot is stationed at the tipper), Tip in Process (green when gripper takes hold of a tote until released), Tipper Clear (green when gripper is open), Tipper Faulted (green if tipper currently has a fault).

content.text: Use the primary operator HMI screen "Visu_MCP_Dual" (Tipper Machine Control Panel) to reset the tipper system after a fault (RESET → CYCLE START) or after an E-stop (ESTOP RESET → AUTO → CYCLE START). Active buttons are indicated by illuminated green bars.

structured_payload.title: Restart Tipper Cycle After Fault or E-Stop Using Visu_MCP_Dual Buttons
structured_payload.summary: Use the primary operator HMI screen "Visu_MCP_Dual" (Tipper Machine Control Panel) to reset the tipper system after a fault (RESET → CYCLE START) or after an E-stop (ESTOP RESET → AUTO → CYCLE START). Active buttons are indicated by illuminated green bars.
structured_payload.when_to_use: When the tipper system needs to be reset and the tipper operation cycle restarted after a fault or after an E-stop, using the primary operator screen "Visu_MCP_Dual".
not_for: Do not use this procedure to jog the tipper. The screen notes that only maintenance personnel should jog the tipper.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the RESET / ESTOP RESET and AUTO / CYCLE START button sequence on the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen and verify the expected restart behavior.
safety_notes: Only maintenance personnel should jog the tipper (JOG is maintenance-only per the screen description).

roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Navigate to the Visu_Alarm screen, load alarm history using SHOW HISTORY, and record the relevant alarm entry/entries and timestamps for the tipper fault being investigated.

content.text: On the Operator Station HMI (VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen), use the VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” button to copy Machine Data parameters from the opposite tipper to the selected axis (Z1, A1, Z2, or A2).

structured_payload.title: Use VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” to copy axis parameters to the selected axis
structured_payload.summary: On the Operator Station HMI (VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen), use the VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” button to copy Machine Data parameters from the opposite tipper to the selected axis (Z1, A1, Z2, or A2).
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when you need to update VISU_MDS Machine Data parameters for a selected axis by copying the corresponding parameters from the other tipper using the VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” function.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for motor replacement commissioning/alignment steps; the manual states Machine Data parameters generally do not require changing unless a motor is replaced.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the VISU_MDS axis selection and press “COPY FROM OPPOSITE”, then verify the Machine Data values updated for the selected axis.
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU access to the VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen

steps.title: Press “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” to copy parameters to the selected axis
steps.purpose: Copy Machine Data parameters from the other tipper to the selected axis.
steps.instruction: Click the “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” button on the VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen.
steps.expected_result: The Machine Data values for the selected axis update to reflect the copied parameters from the opposite tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: After the button press, the selected axis’ Machine Data values change from their prior values to match the copied set (for the parameters that are intended to match machine-to-machine).
steps.failure_condition: Pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” results in no visible change to the selected axis Machine Data values.

actions.exact_action: Click the “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” button to copy parameters to the selected axis from the other tipper.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Use the COPY FROM OPPOSITE button to copy parameters to the selected axis from the other tipper.

steps.title: Verify the selected axis Machine Data values updated
steps.purpose: Confirm the copy operation updated the expected Machine Data IDs/fields for the selected axis.
steps.instruction: On the VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen, verify that the Machine Data values for the selected axis updated to the copied values. Check the listed IDs/fields including: OT Minus (ID 1), Tote Pickup Position (ID 5), travel opposite positions (IDs 6 and 7), Tote Dump Position (ID 8), Soft Travel Lim Pos (ID 9), OT Pos (ID 10), Base Speed for AutoCycle (ID 11) and Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (ID 12), Jog Speed (ID 13) and Jog Acceleration (ID 14), and Home/offset/homing parameters (IDs 20–24).
steps.expected_result: The selected axis shows updated values for the checked Machine Data IDs/fields after the copy.
steps.healthy_condition: The Machine Data values for the selected axis reflect the copied parameters from the other tipper for the parameters that should match machine-to-machine (with the manual-stated exceptions).
steps.failure_condition: One or more of the checked Machine Data IDs/fields do not change as expected after the copy, or mismatches persist after copy.

actions.label: Check Machine Data IDs/fields
actions.exact_action: Verify on the VISU_MDS screen that the Machine Data values for the selected axis updated to the copied values (check the listed IDs/fields such as OT Minus (ID 1), Tote Pickup Position (ID 5), travel opposite positions (IDs 6 and 7), Tote Dump Position (ID 8), Soft Travel Lim Pos (ID 9), OT Pos (ID 10), Base Speed/Acc-Dec for AutoCycle (IDs 11–12), Jog Speed/Acceleration (IDs 13–14), and Home/offset/homing parameters (IDs 20–24)).

stop_or_escalate_if: If mismatches persist after copy, re-check the axis selection and the specific Machine Data IDs shown on VISU_MDS.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: From machine to machine, the following data values should match: ID 1 OT Minus; ID 5 Tote Pickup Position; ID 6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position; ID 7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position; ID 8 Tote Dump Position; ID 9 Soft Travel Lim Pos; ID 10 OT Pos; ID 11 Base Speed for AutoCycle; ID 12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle; ID 13 Jog Speed; ID 14 Jog Acceleration; and ID 20 Home Position; ID 21 Home Offset; ID 22 Homing Speed; ID 23 Homing CAM Speed; ID 24 Homing Acceleration.
Exceptions for matching values: MD5 Tote Pickup Position will be unique for every machine and every axis; MD21 Home Offset will be unique for every machine and every axis.

success_criteria: After pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE”, the VISU_MDS Machine Data values for the selected axis reflect the copied parameters from the opposite tipper.

The checked Machine Data IDs/fields on VISU_MDS show updated values consistent with the manual’s machine-to-machine matching list, accounting for the stated exceptions (MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset).
healthy_conditions: VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen shows axis parameters for Z1, A1, Z2, and A2.
After “COPY FROM OPPOSITE”, the selected axis Machine Data values update (for the parameters intended to match machine-to-machine).
MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset are treated as exceptions (unique per machine and axis) when evaluating whether values match.
failure_conditions: Pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” produces no visible change to the selected axis Machine Data values.
After copy, one or more expected Machine Data IDs/fields do not update or remain mismatched (excluding the manual-stated exceptions).
escalation_guidance: Stop and escalate if pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” results in no visible change to the selected axis Machine Data values.
If mismatches persist after copy, re-check the axis selection and the specific Machine Data IDs shown on VISU_MDS, then escalate if still unresolved.
