steps.purpose: Determine whether the Machine Data values that “should match” are consistent between machines for the same axis.
steps.instruction: Compare the Machine Data values between machines for the selected axis. The following data values should match between machines: ID 0 Axis Name, ID 1 OT Minus, ID 5 Tote Pickup Position, ID 6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 8 Tote Dump Position, ID 9 Soft Travel Lim Pos, ID 10 OT Pos, ID 11 Base Speed for AutoCycle (steps/min), ID 12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (steps/min^2)/10, ID 13 Jog Speed, and ID 14 Jog Acceleration, plus ID 20 Home Position, ID 21 Home Offset, ID 22 Homing Speed, ID 23 Homing CAM Speed, and ID 24 Homing Acceleration.
steps.expected_result: For the selected axis, you can identify which Machine Data IDs match and which IDs differ between the two machines being compared.
steps.healthy_condition: All compared Machine Data values match between machines for the selected axis, except for the documented exceptions (MD5 and MD21).
steps.failure_condition: Any Machine Data ID other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) differs between machines for the same axis.

actions.label: Compare values between machines
actions.exact_action: Compare the values between machines for the parameters that “should match” and note any mismatches.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any mismatch is found for any Machine Data ID other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: From machine to machine, the following data values should match: ID 0 Axis Name, ID 1 OT Minus, ID 5 Tote Pickup Position, ID 6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 8 Tote Dump Position, ID 9 Soft Travel Lim Pos, ID 10 OT Pos, ID 11 Base Speed for AutoCycle (steps/min), ID 12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (steps/min^2)/10, ID 13 Jog Speed, ID 14 Jog Acceleration, ID 20 Home Position, ID 21 Home Offset, ID 22 Homing Speed, ID 23 Homing CAM Speed, ID 24 Homing Acceleration.

steps.title: Apply the documented exceptions for MD5 and MD21
steps.purpose: Avoid false positives by treating the two documented unique parameters as expected differences.
steps.instruction: When comparing machine-to-machine values for the selected axis, apply these exceptions: (1) MD5 Tote Pickup Position is expected to be unique for every machine and every axis, and (2) MD21 Home Offset is expected to be unique for every machine and every axis.
steps.expected_result: Any differences observed in MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) are treated as expected and not counted as faults.
steps.healthy_condition: MD5 and MD21 may differ between machines for the same axis, while all other IDs match.
steps.failure_condition: You treat MD5 or MD21 differences as a fault, or you fail to escalate when a non-exception ID differs.

actions.label: Check exception fields
actions.exact_action: Apply the two documented exceptions: MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not treat differences in MD5 Tote Pickup Position or MD21 Home Offset as a fault; they are expected to be unique per machine and axis.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: There are two exceptions for matching values: MD5 Tote Pickup Position will be unique for every machine and every axis; MD21 Home Offset will be unique for every machine and every axis.

steps.title: Repeat the comparison for the remaining axes (Z1/A1/Z2/A2) and conclude

steps.expected_result: You have a pass/fail determination for each axis based on whether any non-exception Machine Data ID differs between machines.
steps.healthy_condition: For each axis, all Machine Data values match between machines except MD5 and MD21, which may differ.
steps.failure_condition: At least one axis has a mismatch in a Machine Data ID other than MD5 or MD21.

actions.label: Repeat for each axis
actions.exact_action: Repeat for the other axis selections (Z1, A1, Z2, A2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any parameter other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) is different between machines for the same axis.

steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (when necessary) to access the motor area.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete and the motor/A-axis PCA area is accessible.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not removed when required for access, or hardware is removed incorrectly.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove the four M3 socket-head screws holding the two FFC clamps
steps.purpose: Release the old FFC from the A-axis PCA by removing the clamp fasteners.
steps.instruction: Starting at the A-axis PCA, remove the four (4) M3 socket-head screws holding the two (2) FFC clamps.
steps.expected_result: All four M3 socket-head screws are removed and the FFC clamps are released from the A-axis PCA.
steps.healthy_condition: The two FFC clamps are loosened/removed such that the old FFC can be unplugged.
steps.failure_condition: Any of the four M3 screws remain installed or clamps are not fully released.

actions.label: Identify A-axis PCA clamp screws
actions.exact_action: Starting at the A-axis PCA, remove the four (4) M3 socket-head screws holding the two (2) FFC clamps.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged or clamps cannot be resecured with the M3 socket-head screws, stop and escalate for further guidance.

steps.title: Unplug the old FFC from the A-axis PCA connection point
steps.purpose: Remove the defective/old flat-flex cable so the replacement can be installed.
steps.instruction: Unplug the old FFC from the A-axis PCA connection point.
steps.expected_result: Old FFC is fully unplugged from the A-axis PCA connection point.
steps.healthy_condition: FFC is removed without damaging the connector/clamps.
steps.failure_condition: FFC remains partially connected or cannot be unplugged.

actions.label: Unplug old FFC
actions.exact_action: Unplug the old FFC from the A-axis PCA connection point.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged, stop and escalate for further guidance.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.14.1 step 4: "Unplug the old FFC from the A-axis PCA connection point."

steps.title: Plug in the new replacement FFC
steps.purpose: Install the correct replacement flat-flex cable into the A-axis PCA connection point.
steps.instruction: Plug in the new FFC.
steps.expected_result: New FFC is seated/connected at the A-axis PCA connection point.
steps.healthy_condition: FFC is properly connected such that clamps can be reinstalled.
steps.failure_condition: FFC does not seat/connect or cannot be clamped down.

actions.label: Install new FFC
actions.exact_action: Plug in the new FFC.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not install the wrong controller hardware: left and right ClearLink controllers have the same hardware but are not interchangeable because IP addresses differ; ensure the correct controller/FFC assembly is installed as applicable.
If the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged or clamps cannot be resecured with the M3 socket-head screws, stop and escalate for further guidance.

steps.title: Reinstall the FFC clamps and secure with the four M3 socket-head screws

steps.healthy_condition: All four M3 socket-head screws are installed and clamps hold the FFC in place.

actions.label: Secure clamps with M3 screws
actions.exact_action: reinstall the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws.

stop_or_escalate_if: If clamps cannot be resecured with the M3 socket-head screws, stop and escalate for further guidance.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.14.1 step 6: "Plug in the new FFC and reinstall the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws."

structured_payload.title: 7.3.20.1 Idler Pulley Assembly Replacement - Removal (LOTO, side panel access, carriage positioning)
structured_payload.summary: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor, then manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base and secure them with M6 socket-head screws to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this procedure to prepare the OptiSweep tipper for the idler pulley assembly replacement removal steps by completing LOTO, gaining motor access via the station side panel (if necessary), and securing the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop when belt tension is released.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Executes LOTO, performs side panel removal (if necessary), positions the A-axis/counterbalance, and threads the M6 socket-head screws to prevent dropping.
safety_notes: Do not proceed without completing LOTO (escalation note).
The procedure includes securing the A-axis and counterbalance to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to the station side panel securing screws and motor area
Replacement part: Idler pulley assembly (for later steps in the full replacement procedure)

system_preconditions: Tipper is ready for Operator Station Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) per the referenced procedure on page 2.
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure referenced on page 2 (name as given in this manual section).

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before any side panel removal or manual positioning work.
steps.instruction: Complete LOTO on the tipper using the procedure referenced as "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2.
steps.expected_result: Tipper is LOTO.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed for the tipper before proceeding to side panel removal or manual positioning.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO is not completed and work proceeds anyway.

actions.label: Complete Operator Station Lockout/Tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not proceed without completing LOTO.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel (if necessary) to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area for the subsequent A-axis/counterbalance positioning and belt-tension-related work.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (if needed) to access the motor.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel is removed and the motor area is accessible.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not removed when needed for motor access, or removal is attempted without LOTO.

actions.label: Remove nine self-tapping side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and ensure LOTO is complete before proceeding with any side panel removal.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes
steps.purpose: Set the A-axis/counterbalance to the correct safe position so it cannot drop when belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail (as described).
steps.failure_condition: Carriages cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.

actions.label: Manually position carriages between threaded holes
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, stop and escalate before releasing belt tension.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 3. Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Mechanically secure the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop once belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screws are installed below both carriages (as described).
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws are not threaded into the holes below both carriages.

actions.label: Install M6 socket-head screws below carriages
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance was not positioned between the threaded holes as described (the screws are intended to prevent dropping).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 3. ... Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

success_criteria: Tipper is LOTO.
Station side panel is removed (if necessary) to access the motor.
A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
healthy_conditions: LOTO completed before any physical access/removal.
Carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
M6 socket-head screws are installed below both carriages.
failure_conditions: LOTO not completed.
Carriages cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.
M6 socket-head screws not installed below both carriages.
escalation_guidance: If the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, stop and escalate before releasing belt tension.

structured_payload.title: Set Z-Axis Home Position (Tipper Commissioning)
structured_payload.summary: On the OptiSweep tipper HMI, use the "Visu_MDs" (F2) screen to enter the previously recorded Z-axis "Home Offset" values into the "New Value" column for each Z-axis, press UPDATE to apply, and repeat for the other Z-axis.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use during tipper commissioning when you need to set each tipper Z-axis "Home Offset" to the previously recorded value and confirm the update on the "Visu_MDs" screen.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute the HMI parameter update on the "Visu_MDs" (F2) screen by entering the recorded "Home Offset" values and confirming with UPDATE.

steps.title: Navigate to the "Visu_MDs" (F2) screen
steps.purpose: Open the HMI screen where the Z-axis "Home Offset" values are entered and updated.
steps.instruction: On the OptiSweep HMI, navigate to the "Visu_MDs" screen using the F2 function key.
steps.expected_result: The "Visu_MDs" screen is displayed and ready for editing the Z-axis "Home Offset" settings.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Visu_MDs" screen is active (F2) and shows the "Home Offset" setting(s) with an editable "New Value" column.
steps.failure_condition: The "Visu_MDs" screen does not open, or the "Home Offset" "New Value" fields are not available for editing.

actions.label: Open Visu_MDs (F2)

steps.title: Enter recorded Z-axis "Home Offset" values into "New Value"
steps.purpose: Apply the previously recorded "Home Offset" values to each Z-axis via the "New Value" column.
steps.instruction: For each Z-axis, locate the "Home Offset" setting and enter the previously recorded value into the "New Value" column.
steps.expected_result: Each Z-axis "Home Offset" field shows the entered value in the "New Value" column.
steps.healthy_condition: All intended Z-axis "Home Offset" entries are present in the "New Value" column (one per Z-axis) and match the previously recorded values.
steps.failure_condition: A "Home Offset" value cannot be entered, or the entered "New Value" does not match the previously recorded value for that Z-axis.

actions.label: Set Home Offset New Value
actions.exact_action: For each Z-axis, for the "Home Offset" setting, enter the value recorded in the previous procedure in the "New Value" column.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.23.8: SET Z-AXIS HOME POSITION 2. For each Z-axis, for the "Home Offset" setting, enter the value recorded in the previous procedure in the "New Value" column.

steps.title: Press UPDATE to confirm the change
steps.purpose: Apply the entered "Home Offset" "New Value" to the system.
steps.instruction: Press UPDATE to confirm the change for the Z-axis.
steps.expected_result: After pressing UPDATE, the "Home Offset" setting reflects the entered "New Value" for that Z-axis.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Home Offset" value shown on the "Visu_MDs" screen updates to the newly entered value after UPDATE.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing UPDATE does not apply the entered "New Value" (the "Home Offset" value does not change as expected).

actions.label: Confirm update
actions.exact_action: Press UPDATE to confirm the change.

stop_or_escalate_if: If UPDATE does not apply the entered "New Value" (values do not change as expected), stop and escalate for support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.23.8: SET Z-AXIS HOME POSITION 3. Press UPDATE to confirm the change.

steps.title: Repeat for the other Z-axis
steps.purpose: Ensure all Z-axis "Home Offset" settings are updated to their recorded values.
steps.instruction: Repeat the "Home Offset" "New Value" entry and UPDATE confirmation for the other Z-axis.
steps.expected_result: The other Z-axis "Home Offset" reflects its entered "New Value" after pressing UPDATE.
steps.healthy_condition: Both Z-axis "Home Offset" values on the "Visu_MDs" screen match the previously recorded values after their respective UPDATE actions.
steps.failure_condition: The other Z-axis does not update after UPDATE, or its "Home Offset" does not match the previously recorded value.

actions.label: Update other Z-axis
actions.exact_action: Repeat for the other Z-axis.

stop_or_escalate_if: If UPDATE does not apply the entered "New Value" for the other Z-axis (values do not change as expected), stop and escalate for support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.23.8: SET Z-AXIS HOME POSITION 4. Repeat for the other Z-axis.

success_criteria: After pressing UPDATE for each Z-axis, the "Home Offset" setting(s) on the "Visu_MDs" screen reflect the entered "New Value" values.

failure_conditions: Pressing UPDATE does not change the "Home Offset" value to match the entered "New Value" for a Z-axis.
escalation_guidance: If UPDATE does not apply the entered "New Value" (values do not change as expected), stop and escalate for support.

content.text: On the OptiSweep tipper operator station HMI, use the Visu_MCP_Dual (F3) jogging screen to jog the Z-axis upward using the '+' button until it is as close as possible to the overtravel switch without the motor hitting the frame. If the motor reaches the overtravel switch, move it back down approximately 1/3 in.

structured_payload.title: Remove and unplug Limit/Home sensor (A-axis or Z-axis)
structured_payload.summary: LOTO the tipper, unplug and remove a defective Limit/Home proximity sensor (A-axis or Z-axis), and route the sensor cable through the wire routing hole for replacement.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when a Limit/Home proximity sensor is defective and must be removed (A-axis sensor or Z-axis sensor) so it can be replaced, including preparing the cable routing for the new sensor.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: perform LOTO and physical sensor removal/unplugging and cable routing preparation.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO of the tipper before unplugging/removing the sensor.
access_or_tools_needed: Replacement part: Limit sensor or home sensor
Access to tipper for LOTO and to sensor connection points (PCA near A-axis motor or CLINK controller inside control box)

system_preconditions: Tipper is available for lockout/tagout (LOTO).
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout (referenced on page 2 in the manual section).

visual_references.description: A-Axis PCA connections showing A-axis wire routing through the wire routing hole and fastening with an M3 button-head screw; also shows where A-axis sensor wires plug into the PCA.
Z-Axis CLINK connections showing Z-axis wires dropping through the column and out the lower grommet into the control box and plugging into I/O1, DI6, or DI7.
Flat-Flex Cable (FFC) diagram at the A-axis PCA showing the M3 socket-head screws and FFC clamps (useful for understanding the A-axis PCA connection area).
CLINK controller diagram showing the controller box and cable connections (useful for understanding the Z-axis sensor connection point inside the control box).

steps.title: Identify whether the defective sensor is A-axis or Z-axis
steps.purpose: Ensure you unplug the sensor from the correct connection point (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box).
steps.instruction: Use the sensor location guidance to determine whether the defective Limit/Home sensor is an A-axis sensor or a Z-axis sensor.
steps.expected_result: You can classify the sensor as either A-axis or Z-axis based on its location/connection point.
steps.healthy_condition: A-axis sensor is identified as being plugged into a printed circuit assembly (PCA) near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensor is identified as being plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine whether the sensor is A-axis or Z-axis, or you identify the wrong connection point type.

actions.label: Classify sensor location
actions.exact_action: Review sensor locations on the previous page ("Sensors" section) to identify whether the sensor is A-axis or Z-axis.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor connection point cannot be identified (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box), stop and re-check sensor location guidance.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: NOTE: See "Sensors" on the previous page for sensor locations. A-axis sensors are plugged into a PCA near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Make the tipper safe for unplugging/removal work.
steps.instruction: LOTO the tipper using the manual’s Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out prior to unplugging the sensor.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is applied before any sensor unplugging/removal actions.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to unplug/remove the sensor without LOTO.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Unplug the sensor
steps.purpose: Disconnect the sensor electrically so it can be removed from its mounting location.
steps.instruction: Unplug the sensor from its connection point.
steps.expected_result: The sensor is unplugged from its connection point (PCA near A-axis motor for A-axis; CLINK controller inside control box for Z-axis).
steps.healthy_condition: Unplugging is performed at the correct connection point for the identified sensor type.
steps.failure_condition: You unplug from an incorrect location or cannot access/unplug the sensor due to misidentification.

actions.label: Unplug sensor
actions.exact_action: Unplug the sensor.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor connection point cannot be identified (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box), stop and re-check sensor location guidance.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 2. Unplug the sensor. A-axis sensors are plugged into a printed circuit assembly (PCA) near the A-axis motor. Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.

steps.title: Remove the sensor mounting screw and feed the sensor through the wire routing hole
steps.purpose: Release the sensor from its mounting location and free the cable for removal.
steps.instruction: Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place, then feed the sensor through the hole where the wire is routed.
steps.expected_result: The M3 button-head screw is removed and the sensor is fed through the wire routing hole.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is loosened and can be pulled away from the column area (A-axis) or pulled from the column (Z-axis) after feeding through the wire routing hole.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor remains secured because the M3 screw was not removed or the sensor cannot be fed through the wire routing hole.

actions.label: Remove M3 screw and feed sensor
actions.exact_action: Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed it through the hole in which the wire is routed.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 3. Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed it through the hole in which the wire is routed.

steps.title: Pull the sensor out (A-axis vs Z-axis handling)
steps.purpose: Complete physical removal of the defective sensor from its mounting location.
steps.instruction: If removing an A-axis sensor, pull the sensor away from the column area; if removing a Z-axis sensor, pull the sensor from the column. If the A-axis sensor is defective, cut the wire tie if needed.
steps.expected_result: The defective sensor is removed from its mounting location: A-axis sensor pulled away from the column area; Z-axis sensor pulled from the column.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is free and removed without damaging the cable routing; any required wire tie is cut to allow removal.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor does not pull free (wire tie may need to be cut) or removal damages cable routing.

actions.label: Pull A-axis sensor
actions.exact_action: A defective A-axis sensor is pulled away, but the wire tie may need to be cut.

actions.label: Pull Z-axis sensor
actions.exact_action: Pull the Z-axis sensor from the column.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor does not pull free, cut the wire tie (noted as potentially required for a defective A-axis sensor).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 4. Pull the Z-axis sensor from the column. A defective A-axis sensor is pulled away, but the wire tie may need to be cut.

steps.title: Optional: use the new sensor to pull through cable routing
steps.purpose: Make cable routing for the replacement easier by using the new sensor to pull the cable through the routing path.
steps.instruction: If beneficial, connect the new sensor to the one being replaced to pull through the cable routing so it is routed properly and easier.
steps.expected_result: Cable routing is prepared so the replacement sensor can be routed properly through the wire routing path.
steps.healthy_condition: Replacement sensor cable can be routed through the hole/wire routing path without excessive resistance.
steps.failure_condition: Cable routing is not properly guided through the routing hole/path, increasing risk of pinching or incorrect routing.

actions.label: Connect sensors for pull-through
actions.exact_action: it may be beneficial to connect the new sensor to the one being replaced to pull through the cable routing so it is routed properly and easier.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: NOTE: it may be beneficial to connect the new sensor to the one being replaced to pull through the cable routing so it is routed properly and easier.

success_criteria: Defective Limit/Home sensor is unplugged and removed from its mounting location (A-axis sensor pulled away from column area; Z-axis sensor pulled from the column).
Sensor cable is routed through the hole where the wire is routed, with any wire tie cut as needed.
healthy_conditions: A-axis sensor removal: sensor pulled away from the column area; wire tie cut only if needed for a defective A-axis sensor.
Z-axis sensor removal: sensor pulled from the column.
failure_conditions: Sensor does not pull free and wire tie was not cut when needed (A-axis defective sensor case).
Sensor connection point cannot be identified (PCA near A-axis motor vs CLINK controller inside control box).
escalation_guidance: If you cannot identify whether the sensor is A-axis or Z-axis, stop and re-check the sensor location guidance referenced by the manual’s Sensors page.
If the sensor cannot be removed after cutting the wire tie (when applicable), stop and escalate to maintenance/engineering support for further inspection of the mounting and routing.
missing_details: The provided source section contains removal steps and tool/PPE requirements; installation/replacement steps are not present in the provided text.
The manual references a separate "Sensors" page for sensor locations; the packet does not include that page’s image/OCR for direct step-level verification.

content.text: LOTO the OptiSweep tipper, replace the damaged end stop assembly using two new M8x40 socket-head screws with Loctite®, and inspect the opposite end stop for damage (end stops typically work in pairs).

structured_payload.title: Replace OptiSweep End Stop Assembly (End Stops typically work in pairs)
structured_payload.summary: LOTO the OptiSweep tipper, replace the damaged end stop assembly using two new M8x40 socket-head screws with Loctite®, and inspect the opposite end stop for damage (end stops typically work in pairs).
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when an OptiSweep tipper end stop assembly is damaged and needs replacement, and you must also check the opposite end stop because end stops typically work in pairs.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform physical lockout/tagout (LOTO), remove and replace the end stop assembly, and inspect the opposite end stop for damage.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO of the tipper before removing the side panel (if necessary) and before removing/mounting end stop hardware.
access_or_tools_needed: Replacement parts: End stop; two (2) M8x40 socket-head cap screws (per end stop)
Tools: 3/8-in. wrench or socket, 6-mm hex wrench, Loctite®

system_preconditions: Tipper is available for LOTO (Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure on page 2).
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

visual_references.description: Figure 7-12: End Stop diagram showing the end stop assembly and the M8x40 socket-head screws used for mounting (top/bottom end stops).

steps.title: Review the end-stop pairing note and collision implication
steps.purpose: Ensure you inspect the opposite end stop because end stops typically work in pairs.
steps.instruction: Before starting the physical work, apply the pairing logic: a collision at the bottom often indicates a collision at the top; therefore, a damaged bottom end stop suggests one of the top end stops is also damaged (exception: belt failure).
steps.expected_result: You are prepared to inspect the opposite end stop for damage after replacing the damaged one.
steps.healthy_condition: Your plan includes checking the opposite end stop for damage, consistent with the pairing note.
steps.failure_condition: You replace only the damaged end stop without checking the opposite end stop, despite the pairing note.

actions.label: Apply pairing logic
actions.exact_action: Note that the end stops typically work in pairs. In most cases, a collision at the bottom means there is also a collision at the top.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Note that the end stops typically work in pairs. In most cases, a collision at the bottom means there is also a collision at the top… An exception to this could be in the event of a belt failure.”

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Make the tipper safe for mechanical replacement work.
steps.instruction: LOTO the tipper using the “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” procedure on page 2.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out per the Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure before you remove hardware.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place before side panel removal (if necessary) and before removing the end stop screws.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to remove the side panel or end stop screws without LOTO.

actions.label: Lockout/Tagout tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).”

steps.title: Remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the end stop mounting hardware.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws of the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (only if necessary) and the motor area is accessible for end stop screw removal.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete and you can reach the end stop mounting screws with the tipper still under LOTO.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the end stop mounting screws because the side panel was not removed when needed, or you proceed without maintaining LOTO.

actions.label: Remove side panel
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: If access to the motor is not possible without removing the side panel, ensure LOTO is maintained before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.”

steps.title: Remove the two M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops
steps.purpose: Detach the damaged end stop assembly from the tipper.
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place.
steps.expected_result: The end stop assembly is unfastened and can be removed/replaced.
steps.healthy_condition: Both M8 socket-head screws are removed and the end stop is free from its mounting points.
steps.failure_condition: Only one screw is removed, screws are stripped, or you remove hardware without LOTO.

actions.label: Remove end stop screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “3. Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place.”

steps.title: Mount the new end stop using two new M8x40 socket-head screws with Loctite®
steps.purpose: Install the replacement end stop assembly securely.
steps.instruction: Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and Loctite®.
steps.expected_result: New end stop is mounted using two new M8 socket-head screws with Loctite®.
steps.healthy_condition: Both mounting screws are installed on the new end stop and Loctite® is used as specified.
steps.failure_condition: Old screws are reused, Loctite® is omitted, or the end stop is not seated at the mounting points.

actions.label: Install replacement end stop
actions.exact_action: Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and Loctite®.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Required Tools… Replacement Parts: End stop, two (2) M8x40 socket-head cap screws (per end stop)… Tools Needed: 3/8-in. wrench or socket, 6-mm hex wrench, Loctite®”
“4. Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and Loctite®.”

steps.title: Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary
steps.purpose: Prevent repeat faults by addressing the paired end stop condition.
steps.instruction: Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace it if necessary.
steps.expected_result: Opposite end stop is inspected; if damaged, it is replaced.
steps.healthy_condition: Opposite end stop shows no damage (or is replaced if damage is found).
steps.failure_condition: Opposite end stop is damaged but left unreplaced.

actions.label: Inspect opposite end stop
actions.exact_action: Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the opposite end stop is found damaged, replace it as well (end stops typically work in pairs).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “5. Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary.”

steps.title: Reinstall side panels if necessary and restart the operator station
steps.purpose: Restore the station to service after mechanical replacement.
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary, then re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.expected_result: Side panels are reinstalled (if removed) and the operator station is restarted.
steps.healthy_condition: Station is returned to normal configuration and operator station restart is completed per the referenced procedure.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels are not reinstalled after removal, or operator station is not restarted per the referenced procedure.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “6. Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary. 7. Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).”

success_criteria: Damaged end stop is replaced with a new end stop mounted using two new M8 socket-head screws with Loctite®.
Opposite end stop is checked for damage and replaced if necessary.
Side panels are reinstalled (if removed) and the operator station is restarted.
healthy_conditions: New end stop is mounted using two new M8 socket-head screws with Loctite®.
Opposite end stop is not damaged (or has been replaced if damage was found).
failure_conditions: Opposite end stop remains damaged after inspection.
End stop mounting does not use two new screws and Loctite® as specified.
Side panels are left removed after the replacement.
escalation_guidance: If you cannot access the motor without removing the side panel, maintain LOTO before proceeding.
If the opposite end stop is found damaged, replace it as well (end stops typically work in pairs).

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: End stops (top and bottom) and the M8x40 socket-head cap screws used for mounting; use to identify the end stop assembly location and mounting hardware.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Section 7.3.12 End Stop Assembly Replacement includes required tools/PPE, the pair-collision note, and steps 1-5 for LOTO, optional side panel removal, removing M8 screws, mounting new end stop with Loctite, and checking opposite end stop.
Figure 7-12: End Stop diagram supports identifying the end stop assembly and M8x40 socket-head screws.

image_refs.what_to_look_at: End stops (top and bottom) and the M8x40 socket-head cap screws used for mounting; use to identify the end stop assembly location and mounting hardware.

content.text: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor/valve area, remove the valve cover secured by four M4x50 socket-head screws, and disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the pneumatic valve.

structured_payload.title: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal (LOTO, side panel access, valve cover removal, M8 connector disconnect)
structured_payload.summary: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor/valve area, remove the valve cover secured by four M4x50 socket-head screws, and disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the pneumatic valve.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when removing the pneumatic valve at the OptiSweep tipper station requires LOTO, side panel access, valve cover removal, and disconnecting the valve’s M8 electrical connector (as part of the pneumatic valve replacement/removal task).
not_for: Do not continue if the station side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.
Do not continue if the M8 electrical connector cannot be disconnected from the edge of the valve.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute LOTO and perform the physical removal/disconnection steps (side panel, valve cover screws, and M8 connector).
safety_notes: Apply LOTO to the tipper before starting the removal steps.
access_or_tools_needed: Tools: 2.5-mm hex wrench, 3-mm hex wrench, 5-mm hex wrench, 6-mm hex wrench, 3/8-in. wrench or socket, Loctite®
LOTO capability for the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2)

access_required: On-site physical access to the OptiSweep tipper station side panel and valve cover area
system_preconditions: Tipper is capable of being LOTO’d
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout (page 2)

visual_references.description: Figure 7-9 pneumatic valve maintenance diagram showing valve cover, four M4x50 socket-head screws, and M8 connector location on the valve edge.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out before accessing the motor/valve area.
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper (use the lockout/tagout reference labeled "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).
steps.expected_result: The tipper is LOTO’d.
steps.healthy_condition: Tipper remains in a locked-out state while you proceed to physical removal steps.
steps.failure_condition: You begin side panel/valve cover removal without the tipper being LOTO’d.

actions.label: Apply LOTO to tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove station side panel (if necessary) to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor/valve area by removing the station side panel when required.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (or remains in place if not necessary) and the motor access area is available.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed before attempting to remove the side panel.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal: Step 2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove valve cover screws
steps.purpose: Release the valve cover so the valve and its electrical connector can be accessed.
steps.instruction: Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place.
steps.expected_result: Valve cover is no longer secured by the four (4) M4 socket head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: All four (4) M4 socket head screws are removed from the valve cover.
steps.failure_condition: Valve cover remains secured because one or more of the four (4) M4 socket head screws are still installed.

actions.label: Remove valve cover screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place.

steps.title: Disconnect M8 electrical connector from valve edge
steps.purpose: Disconnect the valve’s electrical connection to complete the removal/disconnection portion of the pneumatic valve removal task.
steps.instruction: Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the valve.

success_criteria: Tipper is LOTO’d.

M8 electrical connector is disconnected from the edge of the pneumatic valve.
healthy_conditions: All nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed before attempting side panel removal.
All four (4) M4 socket head screws are removed from the valve cover.

content.text: Loosely assemble the taper lock bushing into the timing pulley and align all three holes. Thread set screws into the two opposite holes (threads on the pulley half, smooth on the bushing half), then slip the assembly onto the shaft with keyway alignment (if present). Position the pulley 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face using a spacer and an 8-mm hex wrench. Tighten both opposite set screws in alternating small increments until the set screw torque reaches 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb). Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels if removed, then re-start the operator station.
